articles.title: PET/CT radiomics integrating tumour and whole-body composition enhances prognostic prediction in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a multicentre study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate an integrated PET/CT‑based radiomic model that combines tumour characteristics and whole‑body composition features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study included 477 patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent pretreatment [¹⁸F]FDG‑PET/CT. Patients were allocated to training (n = 294), internal validation (n = 74), and external validation (n = 109) cohorts. Primary tumours and whole‑body composition components, including skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, intermuscular adipose tissue and spine, were automatically segmented on PET/CT images. Radiomic features were extracted from both tumour and body‑composition regions. Feature selection and model development were performed using machine learning approaches. A composite clinical-tumour-body composition model was constructed and compared with clinical and tumour‑radiomic models. RESULTS: The integrated model showed superior prognostic performance over individual models, achieving C‑indices of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.770-0.832), 0.716 (95% CI: 0.639-0.797), and 0.732 (95% CI: 0.660-0.796) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The corresponding AUCs for 3‑year PFS prediction were 0.895 (95% CI: 0.858-0.930), 0.831 (95% CI: 0.727-0.923), and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.639-0.895). The model stratified patients into high‑ and low‑risk groups, with significantly different PFS between the two strata across all cohorts (log‑rank P < 0.05). Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility of the integrated model. CONCLUSIONS: A PET/CT‑based radiomic model integrating clinical, tumour, and whole‑body composition features provides robust, externally validated postoperative prognostic stratification for ESCC. This approach may facilitate individualised risk assessment and inform treatment decision‑making.

articles.title: Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging and 2-year Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Mild Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: Background Mild hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) comprises approximately 30%-50% of neonatal encephalopathy cases, yet neurodevelopmental outcomes remain difficult to predict using clinical assessment alone. Purpose To develop and externally test a diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI)-based machine learning model for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with mild HIE. Materials and Methods This prospective four-hospital study consecutively enrolled neonates from November 2019 through November 2023, with 24-month follow-up completed in November 2025. The primary outcome was adverse neurodevelopment at 24 months, defined as any Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, third edition, composite score below 85; cerebral palsy; or epilepsy requiring ongoing treatment. Clinical-only, imaging-only, and combined clinical-imaging models were developed from 49 DKI parameters and seven clinical variables. Model discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and curves were compared with paired DeLong tests and false discovery rate adjustment. Results Overall, 740 neonates were included (mean gestational age, 38.3 weeks ± 1.3 [SD]; 404 [54.6%] female). Adverse outcomes occurred in 182 of 510 development cohort participants (35.7%) and 80 of 230 external test set participants (34.8%). In the external test set, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89, 0.95), with a sensitivity of 86% (69 of 80) and specificity of 85.3% (128 of 150). It exceeded the clinical-only model (AUC, 0.85; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .004) and imaging-only model (AUC, 0.86; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .005). Prespecified risk stratification yielded a negative predictive value of 100% (61 of 61) for low-risk infants and a positive predictive value of 88% (38 of 43) for high-risk infants. Conclusion In neonates with mild HIE, a combined clinical and DKI model demonstrated higher discrimination for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes than did clinical-only or imaging-only models. © The Author(s) 2026. articles.title: Comparative performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT versus contrast-enhanced CT for predicting pCR to neoadjuvant therapy in locally advanced gastric cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare the performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT with that of contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) in predicting pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). METHODS: This post-hoc analysis of a prospective trial finally enrolled 56 patients with LAGC who completed both ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT and CE-CT at baseline and post-NAT and subsequently underwent curative gastrectomy. Pre- and post-NAT PET parameters, including SUVmax, tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), FAPI-avid tumor volume (FTV), and total lesion FAP expression (TLF), were measured, and their percentage changes were calculated. PET parameters were compared, and their predictive performance for pCR was benchmarked against that of RECIST 1.1 based on CE-CT. RESULTS: Baseline FTV and TLF, as well as all post-treatment PET parameters (SUVmax, TBR, FTV, TLF) and their corresponding percentage changes parameters from baseline, were significantly lower in the pCR group than in the non-pCR group (all P < 0.05). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified all the above as significant predictors of pCR. Compared with CE-CT assessed by RECIST 1.1, post-treatment FTV (FTV-post) and post-treatment TLF (TLF-post) showed significantly higher areas under the curve (AUCs; P = 0.010 and P = 0.036, respectively). Among all predictors, TLF-post achieved the highest discriminative ability (AUC, 0.851), with a sensitivity of 88.89%, a specificity of 74.47%, and a negative predictive value of 97.22%. In contrast, RECIST 1.1 demonstrated perfect specificity (100%) but was limited by a markedly low sensitivity (11.11%). CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to systematically compare ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT with CE-CT for predicting pCR after NAT in LAGC. The superior predictive performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET parameters over RECIST 1.1 criteria supports its role as a valuable response assessment tool, with the potential to inform treatment adaptation-particularly by identifying patients with residual disease who may benefit from timely curative-intent surgery. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov. NCT05140746. Registered 8 November 2021 retrospectively.

articles.title: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in indeterminate renal masses and advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma: clinical utility and management impact in a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab is a PET radiotracer targeting carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX), a biomarker highly expressed in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Following the high diagnostic accuracy demonstrated in the phase III ZIRCON trial, this study evaluated the real-world clinical performance and management impact of [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in patients with indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Within an early access program, patients with renal lesions of uncertain origin underwent [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT for noninvasive lesion characterization, while patients with advanced ccRCC were imaged for postoperative assessment, recurrence evaluation, or metastatic restaging. Following intravenous administration of 37 MBq (± 10%) [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab, PET/CT was performed on day 5 post-injection. Findings were correlated with histopathology where available, and their impact on clinical management was assessed retrospectively. RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients (22 men, 6 women; mean age, 71 ± 9 years) were included: 18 with indeterminate renal masses (Group A) and 10 undergoing postoperative, metastatic, or restaging evaluation (Group B). In Group A, PET/CT demonstrated CAIX-positive findings in 10/18 patients (56%) and CAIX-negative findings in 7/18 (39%); one patient showed heterogeneous tracer uptake. Histopathological confirmation was available in 11/18 patients (61%). Within this verified subset, patient-level PET/CT findings were concordant with histopathology, with all CAIX-positive patients (6/6) confirmed as ccRCC and all CAIX-negative patients (5/5) confirmed as non-ccRCC or benign. At the lesion level, however, concordance was incomplete in one patient: four CAIX-avid lesions were identified, two of which were confirmed as ccRCC, while the remaining two corresponded to an angiomyolipoma and normal renal parenchyma. PET/CT findings were associated with a subsequent change in the documented management plan in 11/18 patients (61%; 95% CI, 35.7-82.7%). In the exploratory Group B cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT demonstrated the presence or absence of detectable CAIX-avid findings and contributed to therapeutic and surveillance decisions. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT showed concordance with histopathology in the limited verified subset and was associated with changes in clinical management, supporting further prospective evaluation in indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.

articles.title: Development and preclinical evaluation of CP021, a CD38-targeted cyclic peptide radiotheranostic platform for multiple myeloma.
articles.abstract: Small and disseminated lesions within the bone marrow remain challenging to detect and eradicate in multiple myeloma (MM), highlighting the need for targeted approaches capable of both sensitive imaging and localized radiation delivery. CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells and represents an established target in MM, but CD38-directed radiopharmaceuticals with rapid tumor targeting and favorable pharmacokinetics remain limited. Here, we developed CP021, a high-affinity CD38-targeting cyclic peptide, and evaluated [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 for PET imaging, together with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 and [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 for targeted radionuclide therapy in preclinical MM models.MethodsDOTA-CP021 was labeled with ⁶⁸Ga or ¹⁷⁷Lu and DOTAM-CP021 with ²¹²Pb. Radiochemical properties, PET imaging, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, dosimetry, therapeutic efficacy, and safety were evaluated in MM xenograft models.ResultsAll radioconjugates showed > 95% radiochemical purity and good stability. [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 demonstrated CD38-dependent tumor uptake; at 60 min, uptake in CD38-high MOLP-8 xenografts was 12.35 ± 1.37%ID/g, 1.8- and 3.1-fold higher than in MM.1 S and U266B1 tumors, respectively. [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 produced activity-dependent tumor growth inhibition and prolonged survival. Repeated [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 further improved tumor control, extending median survival to 36.5 and 47 days at cumulative activities of 0.555 and 1.11 MBq, respectively, versus 16 days with PBS (P < 0.001). No overt treatment-related toxicity was observed.ConclusionCP021 provides a versatile CD38-targeted radiotheranostic platform combining rapid molecular imaging with β- and α-particle therapy. Its performance across radionuclides supports further development for detecting and treating CD38-positive MM lesions.

articles.title: Postoperative dual-time-point [18F]Fluorocholine PET imaging in suspected residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma: comparison with [11C]Methionine PET/MRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Detecting residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) by MRI is challenging due to post-surgical or post-radiotherapy tissue remodeling. While [11C]Methionine ([11C]MET) PET demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for RPA, its use is limited to centers with an on-site cyclotron. [18F]Fluorocholine ([18F]FCH) PET, which has shown incidental uptake in pituitary adenomas, may offer a viable alternative. This study compared dual-phase [18F]FCH with [11C]MET PET imaging for localizing suspected residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) and characterizing uptake differences between suspected RPA and pituitary gland remnant (PGR) after surgery. METHODS: This retrospective study included 23 patients addressed during the follow-up of an ablated pituitary adenoma (n = 23). The presence of suspected RPA was determined by multidisciplinary consensus integrating postoperative metabolic imaging, serial MRI follow-up, and biochemical data. Two patients underwent reoperation, in whom histopathological confirmation was available. All patients underwent a standard [11C]MET PET/MRI acquisition (mean activity = 397 ± 51 MBq) and subsequently a 20-min dynamic [18F]FCH PET/MRI acquisition, followed by an additional late static [18F]FCH PET/CT acquisition performed at 40-55 min post-FCH injection (mean activity = 334 ± 77 MBq). RPA and PGR uptake were compared visually and quantitatively using maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) for both tracers. RESULTS: All lesions suspected of representing RPA were visually detected on both early and late [18F]FCH images. In suspected RPA, [18F]FCH uptake was comparable to [11C]MET uptake, with mean SUVmax values of 6.2 ± 2.3 for early (3-20 min post-injection) [18F]FCH PET, 5.1 ± 2.3 for late [18F]FCH PET, and 5.5 ± 1.9 for [11C]MET (p = 0.11 and 0.51, respectively). Both suspected RPA and PGR showed decreasing [18F]FCH uptake over time, with a significantly greater decline in PGR (early PET SUVmax: 5.7 ± 1.5; late PET SUVmax: 3.7 ± 1.1; time-by-region interaction, p < 0.0001). Accordingly, the RPA/PGR SUVmax ratio was significantly lower on early [18F]FCH images than on late [18F]FCH images (p = 0.0014) and [11C]MET images (p < 0.001), whereas it did not differ significantly between late [18F]FCH and [11C]MET images (p > 0.5). CONCLUSION: [18F]FCH PET/MRI demonstrated uptake in lesions suspected of representing RPA, with uptake levels comparable to those observed with [11C]MET PET/MRI. The greater decline in PGR uptake on delayed imaging improved the quantitative RPA/PGR contrast, supporting dual-time-point [18F]FCH PET/MRI as a promising approach for postoperative tissue discrimination. These exploratory findings require prospective validation using an independent reference standard.

articles.title: [18F]DPA714 PET reveals occult glial activation and tracks disease severity in MOGAD: a prospective study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a heterogeneous neuroinflammatory disorder. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity. Translocator protein (TSPO) is a sensitive biomarker of glial activation that can be imaged non-invasively using PET. We aimed to characterize intracranial inflammatory patterns across MOGAD phenotypes using [18F]DPA714 PET/MRI. METHODS: In this prospective study, 32 MOGAD patients and 10 age/sex-matched healthy controls underwent [18F]DPA714 PET/MRI and comprehensive clinical assessment. All participants were confirmed as high-affinity binders for the TSPO radioligand (rs6971 genotyping) and provided written informed consent. Standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR) were quantified; PET‑positivity was defined as SUVR > control Mean SUVR + 2 SD. RESULTS: [18F]DPA714 PET showed significantly higher detection rate than MRI (27/32, 84.38% vs. 16/32, 50.00%; P = 0.007). [18F]DPA714 uptake correlated with mRS and CASE scores at baseline (both P < 0.01), and changes in SUVR correlated with changes in both scores over follow-up (n = 20; P < 0.05 and P < 0.01, respectively). Patients with seizures, sensory disturbances, or cognitive decline showed higher SUVR in corresponding brain regions. Three PET-based subtypes were identified-cortical-predominant, thalamic/limbic system-predominant, and brainstem/cerebellar-predominant, which exhibited distinct clinical and laboratory features. Patients who achieved clinical improvement had higher baseline abnormal [18F]DPA714 uptake intensity and greater post‑treatment SUVR reduction (both P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: In this single-center exploratory study, [18F]DPA714 PET demonstrated a significantly higher positive detection rate than conventional MRI and correlates with disease severity, supporting its potential as a promising imaging biomarker for MOGAD assessment, precise classification and management. articles.title: The autoPET3 challenge: Automated lesion segmentation in whole-body PET/CT - Multitracer multicenter generalization.
articles.abstract: We report the design and results of the third autoPET challenge (MICCAI 2024), which benchmarked automated lesion segmentation in whole-body PET/CT under a compositional generalization setting. Training data comprised 1014 [18F]-FDG PET/CT studies from the University Hospital Tübingen and 597 [18F]/[68Ga]-PSMA PET/CT studies from the LMU University Hospital Munich, the largest publicly available annotated PSMA PET/CT dataset to date. The held-out test set of 200 studies covered four tracer-center combinations, two of which represented unseen compositional pairings. A complementary data-centric award category restricted participants to a fixed baseline model to isolate data handling strategies. Seventeen teams submitted 27 algorithms, predominantly nnU-Net-based 3D networks with PET/CT channel concatenation. The top-ranked algorithm achieved a mean DSC of 0.66, FNV of 3.18 mL, and FPV of 2.78 mL across all four test conditions, improving DSC by 8% and reducing the false-negative volume by 5mL relative to the provided baseline. Ranking was stable across bootstrap resampling and alternative ranking schemes for the top tier. Beyond the benchmark, we provide an in-depth analysis of segmentation performance at the patient and lesion level. Three main conclusions can be drawn: (1) in-domain multitracer PET/CT segmentation is sufficient and likely approaching reader agreement; (2) compositional generalization to unseen tracer-center combinations remains an open problem mainly driven by systematic volume overestimation; (3) heterogeneity and case difficulty drive performance variation substantially more than the choice of algorithm among top-ranked teams.

articles.title: VoxelSlicer: Adaptive Voxel-wise Slicer for Deformable Image Registration.
articles.abstract: Recent progress in neural networks has accelerated deformable image registration (DIR) by amortizing iterative optimization, offering faster results and potential accuracy gains with label supervision. However, existing methods struggle with highly deformed structures (e.g., inter-subject abdominal or intra-subject cardiac scans) and fail to handle complex motions like sliding or respiratory dynamics. This limitation arises from isotropic diffusive pair-wise regularization, which leads to inefficient message passing and oversmoothed boundaries. We propose VoxelSlicer, a novel neural network module inspired by the traditional bilateral grid but enhanced with learnable adaptive filtering. VoxelSlicer enables voxel-wise adaptive filtering, addressing local discontinuities in displacement fields and performs more efficient message passing. This design enables adaptive displacement-cost propagation with a compact parameter footprint and a favorable accuracy-complexity trade-off. Experiments on four realistic datasets and two synthetic datasets with different modalities and input constraints demonstrate VoxelSlicer's competitive registration performance together with favorable accuracy-complexity and accuracy-smoothness trade-offs.

articles.title: Deep Auxiliary Learning via Bilevel Feature Optimization for Label-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Auxiliary learning (AL), which can improve the performance of a primary task by leveraging related auxiliary tasks, is commonly regarded as a special case of multi-task learning. Existing AL approaches typically require manually annotated auxiliary labels, increasing annotation costs, particularly in medical imaging where expert labeling is expensive. In this work, we investigate whether segmentation performance can be improved using auxiliary tasks whose labels are automatically derived from existing segmentation annotations, requiring no additional manual labeling. To address this, we propose a novel auxiliary learning framework, formulated as a bilevel optimization problem. Our method enables effective knowledge transfer between tasks via a feature communication module, enhancing the primary segmentation task. We evaluate the method on three medical image segmentation benchmarks under limited-label settings. The results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior label efficiency. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/FupingWu90/ALBO.

articles.title: Intraindividual comparison of [68​Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 and [18F]FDG PET/CT for initial staging of breast cancer: Additional lesion detection and clinical impact.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare [68​Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 and [18F]FDG PET/CT for initial staging of breast cancer and assess the incremental clinical impact of FAPI findings. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 83 patients with newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer who underwent both examinations within 7 days before treatment. Patient- and lesion-level detection, paired SUVₘₐₓ, histology-specific FDG non-detection, stage migration, additional biopsy, treatment modification, and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated using a composite reference standard. Generalised estimating equations accounted for within-patient lesion clustering. RESULTS: Patient-level positivity was 98.8% (82/83) for FAPI and 91.6% (76/83) for FDG (two-sided exact McNemar p = 0.031). FAPI detected 98.7% (235/238) of reference-positive lesions versus 67.2% (160/238) with FDG (p < 0.001); 76 lesions were FAPI-positive/FDG-negative and one was FDG-positive/FAPI-negative. Among 159 matched lesions, median SUVₘₐₓ was 12.10 for FAPI and 3.90 for FDG (p < 0.001). FDG non-detection was more frequent in invasive lobular carcinoma than in invasive ductal carcinoma/no special type (49.0% vs 30.1%; clustered odds ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.004-4.54; p = 0.049). FAPI findings resulted in stage migration in 19.3%, additional biopsy in 18.1%, and treatment modification in 21.7% of patients. FAPI-only disease was not significantly associated with PFS (p = 0.343). CONCLUSION: [68​Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT detected substantially more breast, nodal, and osseous lesions than [18F]FDG PET/CT and provided verified findings that altered staging and management. FAPI PET/CT may serve as a complementary initial-staging modality, particularly when FDG avidity is low; prospective multicentre validation is required.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Single-sample-calibrated image-derived pharmacokinetics of the PD-L1-targeted tracer [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 using total-body PET: Beyond conventional venous blood sampling.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility and additional value of total-body PET image-derived pharmacokinetics over venous blood-sampling method in investigating non-tumor tissue and lesion kinetics of the PD-L1-targeted tracer [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 in patients with malignant tumors. METHODS: Patients with solid tumors underwent a 60-min dynamic total-body PET acquisition following [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 injection, and a 20-min static scan at 120 min post-injection, accompanied by serial venous blood sampling. Systemic PK parameters were estimated via noncompartmental analysis based on time-concentration curves from venous blood sampling and image-derived venous vascular regions using a single-sample calibration, and the PK parameters obtained from the two methods were compared. To characterize kinetic parameters, time-activity curves (TACs) of non-tumor tissues and lung lesions were fitted using compartment models. Lesions' kinetic metrics and standardized uptake value (SUV) were compared after stratification by tumor proportion score (TPS; < 50% vs. ≥ 50%). RESULTS: Image-derived maximum concentration (Cmax) was significantly higher and time to Cmax (Tmax) was significantly shorter than those obtained from venous blood sampling. No significant between-method differences were observed for the remaining PK parameters, except SVC-derived clearance (CL; 2.35 ± 0.69 vs. 2.69 ± 0.90 L/h, P = 0.016). The relative differences were within 18% for right atrium (RA) and within 19% for superior vena cava (SVC) for these parameters. Lesions with high TPS (≥ 50%) demonstrated significantly elevated K1 (0.51 ± 0.17 vs. 0.11 ± 0.09 mL/cm3/min, P = 0.009) and k2 (6.06 ± 1.76 vs. 2.19 ± 1.60 min-1, P = 0.009) compared to those with low TPS (< 50%). Additionally, dynamic [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 PET provided information on tracer retention in non-tumor tissues and lesions. CONCLUSION: Total-body dynamic PET imaging with a single-sample calibration provides PK data comparable to conventional venous blood sampling while simultaneously characterizing tissue kinetic profiles throughout the body. Additionally, these kinetic parameters may offer complementary value for the stratification of lesion-level PD-L1 expression and the preliminary assessment of immunotherapy response. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This phase I clinical trial was approved by the National Medical Products Administration of China and was registered at www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn  (registry number: CTR20232251).

articles.title: Incidental joint and periarticular [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake in oncological PET/CT: prevalence, distribution, and comparison with [¹⁸F]FDG.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize incidental joint and periarticular [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake in oncological PET/CT, compare it with [¹⁸F]FDG, and define the prevalence and anatomical pattern of visually increased uptake. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 175 consecutive patients with solid tumors underwent [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74-PET/CT. Uptake was assessed in the acromioclavicular (AC), glenohumeral/subacromial (GH/SA), coxofemoral (CF), and sacroiliac (SI) regions. Dual-tracer [¹⁸F]FDG-PET/CT was available in 51 patients. SUVmax and target-to-background ratios (TBRs) were determined, and paired tracer comparisons were performed at the patient level. RESULTS: Increased [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 shoulder uptake occurred in 83/175 patients (47.4%), most frequently involving the GH/SA (68/83, 81.9%) and AC (62/83, 74.7%) regions. CF and SI uptake was observed in 25.7% and 9.1%, respectively. In the dual-tracer cohort, shoulder [¹⁸F]FDG uptake occurred in 12/51 (23.5%) patients. Across evaluated joints, [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake exceeded [¹⁸F]FDG uptake (SUVmax: 6.5 ± 6.3 vs. 2.7 ± 1.5; TBR: 7.0 ± 5.9 vs. 4.6 ± 2.0; both p < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: Joint and periarticular [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake is a frequent incidental finding in oncological PET/CT, particularly in the shoulder region. The incomplete concordance between [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 and [¹⁸F]FDG uptake suggests potentially complementary but non-equivalent imaging information. Prospective multimodal studies are needed to clarify the underlying etiology and clinical relevance of incidental joint-associated FAPI uptake.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Preclinical comparison of B7-H3-targeted 177Lu-radioimmunoconjugates based on self-developed and ifinatamab-based antibodies.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: B7-H3 is a promising theranostic target in lung cancer and other solid tumors, while B7-H3-targeted radiopharmaceuticals still warrant further optimization. We developed 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 using a self-developed humanized anti-B7-H3 monoclonal antibody and compared it with 177Lu-DOTA-huM30, based on a recombinantly expressed antibody with the disclosed sequence of ifinatamab, the antibody component of DS-7300a. METHODS: The anti-B7-H3 monoclonal antibodies hJ42 and huM30 were conjugated with DOTA and radiolabeled with 177Lu for head-to-head evaluation. Radiochemical properties, binding affinity, cellular uptake, and internalization were assessed in vitro. Single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) imaging, biodistribution, therapeutic efficacy, safety, and dosimetry were subsequently evaluated in B7-H3-positive lung cancer patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. RESULTS: Both radioimmunoconjugates showed favorable in vitro stability, with IC50 values of 2.184 nM for 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 and 2.499 nM for 177Lu-DOTA-huM30. Both exhibited time-dependent, B7-H3-specific cellular uptake and efficient internalization. Biodistribution studies in lung cancer PDX models revealed sustained tumor uptake (> 40%ID/g) and favorable tumor/normal tissue ratios, with maximum ratio of approximately 60. SPECT/CT imaging further demonstrated persistent tumor retention in PDX models, whereas background evaluation in non-tumor-bearing B-hB7-H3 humanized mice showed relatively low uptake in normal organs. Single administrations of either 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 or 177Lu-DOTA-huM30 at 7.4 or 14.8 MBq significantly suppressed tumor growth, with no obvious treatment-related toxicity observed during the study period. CONCLUSION: Collectively, 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 enabled specific imaging and effective treatment of B7-H3-positive lung cancer and performed comparably to 177Lu-DOTA-huM30, supporting hJ42 as a promising antibody scaffold for developing B7-H3-targeted radionuclide conjugates.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Association of coronary 68Ga-DOTATATE uptake with CCTA-derived plaque burden in patients without prior cardiovascular events.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: 68Ga-DOTATATE is a positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracer with affinity for somatostatin receptor 2 on pro-inflammatory macrophages. While specific plaque features are linked to inflammatory activity and risk of rupture, the association between plaque composition and functional inflammation remains to be investigated. We aimed to investigate whether 68Ga-DOTATATE can detect plaques features associated with inflammation in asymptomatic patients, and its association with atherosclerotic plaque features. METHODS: Forty participants without prior cardiovascular events with either no significant coronary artery disease (CAD) or extensive CAD underwent 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and were matched 1:1 by age and sex. Coronary tracer uptake was quantified using the maximum target-to-background ratio (TBRmax), calculated by dividing coronary uptake by blood pool activity in the superior vena cava. Associations between plaque features and TBRmax were assessed on a ​per-patient and a per-​plaque level. RESULTS: Mean age was 65 years, 85% were male. On a patient level, higher percent atheroma volume and calcified plaque volume were associated with higher TBRmax. On a plaque level, higher non-calcified and low-density plaque volumes were associated with higher TBRmax (p = 0.020 and p < 0.001), whereas, in contrast to the patient level analyses, calcified plaque volume was associated with a lower TBRmax (p = 0.019). High-risk plaques were associated with higher TBRmax (p = 0.026). CONCLUSIONS: Coronary ⁶⁸Ga-DOTATATE uptake is strongly associated with high-risk plaque features on CCTA on a plaque level. These findings support the potential of ⁶⁸Ga-DOTATATE PET and CCTA-derived parameters for identifying high-risk plaques associated with inflammation in asymptomatic patients.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Whole-body metabolic network alterations and their association with cognitive performance in type 2 diabetes: an 18F-FDG PET/MR study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) disrupts multi-organ glucose metabolism, but systemic inter-organ metabolic coordination and its relevance to cognition remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to construct whole-body metabolic covariance networks using whole-body 18F-FDG PET/MR and explore their associations with cognitive performance in T2DM. METHODS: Twenty-nine patients with T2DM and 46 healthy controls were enrolled. Mean standardized uptake value normalized to lean body mass (SULmean) were extracted from nine cerebral subregions and nine peripheral tissue compartments to calculate whole-body metabolic covariance. These 18 regions were then aggregated into nine major nodes to construct the metabolic connectivity network. Two brain-peripheral decoupling scores were derived from Z-residual covariance features. Correlation and mediation analyses assessed associations between brain-peripheral decoupling and cognition, while four predictive models were compared for classification performance. RESULTS: Although intra-brain metabolic correlations were numerically higher in T2DM patients than in controls across 32 of 36 region pairs, these differences did not survive FDR correction (all q > 0.05). Similarly, brain-peripheral couplings showed only nominal differences between groups and were not FDR-significant (q > 0.05). Network topology analysis indicated different descriptive hub configurations (spleen and pancreas in controls vs. subcutaneous (SAT) and visceral adipose tissue (VAT) in T2DM). Across all participants, the signed decoupling score showed a modest inverse association with MoCA scores in the pooled cohort (r = - 0.31, P = 0.007) that did not reach significance within either subgroup (T2DM: r = - 0.14, P = 0.445). Mediation analysis provided no statistical evidence that brain-peripheral decoupling mediates the association between T2DM status and cognitive outcomes. The multimodal ElasticNet model achieved the highest classification performance (AUC = 0.726, 95% CI 0.602-0.840). CONCLUSIONS: Whole-body metabolic network analysis may provide complementary systems-level information for characterizing T2DM-related metabolic dysregulation and cognitive vulnerability.

articles.title: Excess parenchymal water from MDME-based relaxometry as a quantitative imaging biomarker for distinguishing brain tumors.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the utility of excess parenchymal water (EPW) partial volume, quantified from multi-dynamic multi-echo (MDME)-based relaxometry, in distinguishing brain tumors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 95 patients (61 with grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas, 16 with primary CNS lymphomas (PCNSLs), and 18 with brain metastases) who underwent preoperative MRI including MDME-based sequences between October 2022 and May 2025. EPW partial volume maps were generated using dedicated software. Peritumoral T2 hyperintense regions of interest (ROIs) were defined by subtracting manually drawn ROIs of the enhancing tumor on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images from the whole T2 hyperintense areas. EPW partial volumes were compared among groups using the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc Dunn's tests and Bonferroni correction. Diagnostic performance was assessed by ROC curve analysis. RESULTS: The average EPW partial volume in the peritumoral T2 hyperintense area was significantly lower in grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas (median [IQR], 23.2% [14.6-30.5]) than in brain metastases (30.5% [21.7-37.3]) (p = 0.02). However, no significant differences in EPW partial volumes were observed between gliomas and PCNSLs (p = 0.85), or between PCNSLs and metastases (p = 0.65). The AUC was 0.71 (95% CI, 0.56-0.84) for differentiating gliomas from metastases. Using an EPW cutoff of 27.7%, the sensitivity and specificity were 67% and 71%, respectively. CONCLUSION: EPW partial volume from MDME-based relaxometry was significantly lower in peritumoral areas of grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas than in brain metastases, suggesting its potential as a complementary quantitative biomarker for their differentiation. KEY POINTS: Question Can excess parenchymal water partial volume derived from relaxometry distinguish different types of brain tumors? Findings In this pilot cohort, excess parenchymal water partial volume within peritumoral T2 hyperintense areas was significantly lower in grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas than in brain metastases, despite the modest diagnostic performance. Clinical relevance The average excess parenchymal water partial volume in the peritumoral T2 hyperintense area may complement conventional MRI by providing a quantitative measure that helps differentiate grade 4 adult-type diffuse gliomas from brain metastases.

Longitudinal MR Neurography Changes and Prognostic Significance of Hourglass-like Constrictions in Parsonage-Turner Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Background Hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs) of peripheral nerves are hallmark findings of Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), but their longitudinal characteristics and associations with motor strength and electromyography (EMG) findings, as well as their prognostic value, are unknown. Purpose To delineate longitudinal changes of HGCs and muscle edema with MR neurography (MRN) and to determine their associations with outcomes. Materials and Methods In this prospective study (July 2020 to January 2024), individuals diagnosed with PTS less than 6 months from symptom onset with EMG-confirmed muscle denervation underwent longitudinal assessments (baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months) with physical examination (for muscle strength), EMG, participant-reported outcomes, and 3-T MRN. Two readers independently counted severe and mild HGCs and graded the degree of muscle edema as "severe," "moderate," "mild," or "none." Associations of MRN findings and days from symptom onset with EMG findings and muscle strength were evaluated. Logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to assess whether baseline MRN findings were predictive of follow-up outcomes. Results Among 45 participants (median age, 47.2 years [IQR, 38.7-57.3 years]; 27 male), analyses included 58 affected nerves and 112 affected muscles. Most nerves (90% [52 of 58]) demonstrated HGCs and a median of one to two severe HGCs at baseline, which reduced in frequency (78%-82% [35-37 of 45]) and severity (zero to one) at 12 months. Muscle edema was graded moderate on average at baseline and reduced to mild at 12 months. HGCs were not associated with EMG findings or muscle strength, but a more severe muscle edema grade was associated with increased EMG denervation (odds ratio, 3.19-13.9). HGCs and muscle edema at baseline were not predictive of outcomes, except for muscle edema prediction of self-reported disability at the 3- to 6-month follow-up (β = 4.7-5.9). Conclusion HGCs persisted over the course of 1-year follow-up in PTS but were neither independently predictive of nor associated with muscle strength recovery. Muscle edema grades were associated with EMG denervation. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Evaluation of Total Patent Branch Vessel Ostial Area at Preoperative CT Angiography for Predicting Type II Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
articles.abstract: Background Type II endoleak (T2EL) is a common complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) that may lead to aneurysm sac enlargement. Although guideline-based criteria are used to identify high-risk patients, their predictive accuracy remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the predictive value of preoperative total branch vessel ostial area at CT angiography (CTA) for T2EL after EVAR. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients undergoing EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) between January 2010 and December 2020. After exclusion of other endoleak types, CTA-derived anatomic parameters and outcomes were compared by isolated T2EL status. Total branch vessel ostial area was evaluated using prespecified Cox models and Cox-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis. Discrimination and reproducibility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Of 216 patients in this study (mean age, 66 years ± 7.6 [SD]; 190 male; median follow-up, 4.7 years), 86 (39.8%) developed T2EL. Total branch vessel ostial area showed excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.98-1.00) and was larger in patients with T2EL than in those without T2EL (median, 24.5 vs 11.7 mm2; P < .001). Sac enlargement was more frequent with T2EL (45.3% [39 of 86] vs 12.3% [16 of 130]; P < .001) and was associated with reintervention (hazard ratio [HR], 2.83; P = .003) but not overall survival (HR, 1.76; P = .28). In the fully adjusted Cox model, total branch vessel ostial area was associated with T2EL (HR, 1.06 per 1-mm2 increase [95% CI: 1.04, 1.08]; P < .001). Total branch ostial area showed better discrimination for T2EL than guideline-based criteria (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.82 vs 0.64; P < .001), with a Youden index-derived cutoff of 15.55 mm2. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive continuous association in T2EL risk with increasing ostial area (P < .001). Conclusion Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Liddell in this issue.

articles.title: Hemorrhage Risk in Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations before and after Stereotactic Radiosurgery.
articles.abstract: Background Whether stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is associated with lower hemorrhage risk for unruptured brain arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) during the latency period (ie, from SRS to complete AVM obliteration) remains controversial. Purpose To evaluate whether SRS is associated with lower hemorrhage risk in unruptured brain AVMs during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included 511 patients with unruptured brain AVMs at diagnosis treated with single-session SRS between June 1990 and May 2024. Hemorrhage rates before and after SRS were calculated using the person-year method. A time-dependent Cox proportional hazards model was used to assess the association between SRS and hemorrhage risk. The pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was calculated using the interval between diagnosis and SRS. Results For the 511 patients (median age, 39 years [IQR, 28-52 years]; 306 male patients), the total observation period from diagnosis to SRS or any prior treatment was 1009 person-years, and the pre-SRS hemorrhage rate was 3.4 per 100 person-years (34 hemorrhages). Among 477 patients who underwent SRS without a pre-SRS hemorrhage, 75 patients were lost to follow-up during the latency period, and the median latency period was 33 months, with a total of 1711 person-years. Hemorrhage occurred in 24 patients during the latency period, yielding an overall latency-period hemorrhage rate of 1.4 per 100 person-years. After adjustment for age, nidus volume, and venous drainage, time-dependent Cox proportional hazards analysis showed that SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk in the post-SRS latency period compared with the pre-SRS period, corresponding to a 53% lower hazard (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47 [95% CI: 0.27, 0.83]; P = .009). SRS was also associated with lower hemorrhage risk in lesions treated with SRS following prior surgery or endovascular therapy (hazard ratio, 0.20; P = .01). Conclusion In patients with unruptured brain AVMs, SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Dual-tracer ¹⁸F-FDG and ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT in cardiac spindle cell sarcoma.
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old woman presented with long-standing abdominal distension and unexplained ascites. Serum CA125 levels were significantly elevated. Abdominal CT revealed a cystic lesion in the left adnexal region with massive ascites. To determine the etiology, 18F-FDG PET/CT was performed after fasting for at least 6 h. The adnexal lesion showed no appreciable FDG uptake, favoring a benign cystic lesion. Unexpectedly,​ heterogeneous hypermetabolism was found along the right heart border. Because the interpretation of cardiac FDG findings may be confounded by physiological or nonspecific myocardial uptake, ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT was subsequently performed for further characterization, which revealed a more extensive and conspicuous tracer uptake within the cardiac lesion than FDG PET/CT, more clearly delineating its extent. The patient subsequently underwent partial surgical resection of the cardiac mass with biopsy. Histomorphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of cardiac spindle cell sarcoma with partial myofibroblastic differentiation. This case reports a rare primary cardiac spindle cell sarcoma and highlights the complementary value of FDG and FAPI PET/CT in evaluating primary cardiac malignancies. It also underscores the importance of multimodal imaging in guiding differential diagnosis and clinical management.

articles.title: Case 352: Collision Tumor of Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor and Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
articles.abstract: A 76-year-old woman presented with a 6-month history of progressive anorexia, unintentional weight loss, and heartburn. She reported no abdominal pain, vomiting, gastrointestinal bleeding, or fever but reported intermittent bilateral lower-extremity edema. Physical examination revealed a relatively firm abdominal wall with a palpable upper abdominal mass and no peritoneal signs. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated normocytic anemia (hemoglobin level, 91 g/L; reference range, 115-150 g/L), mild thrombocytosis, no leukocytosis (white blood cell count, 6.24 × 109/L; reference range, 3.5 × 109/L to 9.5 × 109/L), severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin level, 19.5 g/L; reference range, 40.0-55.0 g/L) with low total protein, and electrolyte abnormalities including hyponatremia (sodium level, 128.4 mmol/L; reference range, 137-147 mmol/L) and hypocalcemia (total calcium level, 1.80-1.92 mmol/L; reference range, 2.11-2.52 mmol/L). The D-dimer level was markedly elevated (4900 µg/L [26.8 nmol/L]; reference range, <500 μg/L [<2.7 nmol/L]), whereas serum creatinine level was within the reference range, and serum tumor markers (α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9) were not elevated. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis and fluorine 18 (18F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT were performed.

articles.title: Case 356.
articles.abstract: History A 31-year-old female patient with past medical history of uterine leiomyomas, hypertension, and migraines underwent CT for evaluation of an abdominal wall hernia, and lesions were incidentally discovered (Fig 1). The patient did not report any symptoms other than the bulge due to the hernia. Abdominal examination was negative for tenderness and palpable mass. Past surgical history included multiple myomectomies, cesarean section, and hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy. Laboratory results, including liver function tests, complete blood count, α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9, were within normal limits. The patient underwent MRI for further characterization (Figs 2-5).

articles.title: An immunophenotype-guided interpretable subregional radiomics model for predicting local recurrence-free survival in esophageal squamous cell cancer patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to demonstrate tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) subtypes as prognostic factors for local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) and to develop an interpretable, TIME-guided subregional radiomics model for predicting LRFS. METHODS: 986 ESCC patients from three centers were enrolled. For a subset with available biopsies, multiplex immunofluorescence was used to assess CD3, CD8, and PD-L1 expression, defining prognostic TIME subtypes. Pre-treatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) images were used for tumor segmentation, intratumoral subregion partitioning and radiomic feature extraction. Features associated with TIME subtypes were selected to build a subregional radiomic signature (Subrad signature) for LRFS prediction using an advanced machine learning framework. This signature was integrated with clinical factors to construct a Clinic-Subregional radiomic model (CliSubrad-M). RESULTS: A "PD-L1-low/TILs-high" TIME subtype was identified as an independent favorable prognostic factor for LRFS (HR = 0.34, P < 0.001). The Subrad signature, comprising seven TIME-related features from various subregions, demonstrated robust predictive performance (C-indexes: 0.631-0.637). The integrated CliSubrad-M (built with Random Survival Forest) achieved the best performance, with C-indexes of 0.702 (training), 0.679 (internal testing), 0.653 (external testing1), and 0.625 (external testing2), significantly outperforming the clinical model (all P < 0.05). The model effectively stratified patients into distinct risk groups with significant differences in LRFS. SHAP analysis confirmed the signature's strong contribution and enhanced model interpretability. CONCLUSIONS: The developed interpretable subregional radiomics model, integrating TIME biology with clinical factors, provides a non-invasive tool for predicting LRFS in ESCC received dCRT.

Radiomics and deep learning in locally advanced rectal cancer: linking imaging biology to response-adapted treatment.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer produces a wide range of tumor responses, and total neoadjuvant therapy and watch-and-wait strategies have made response assessment a central task for radiologists. Morphological MRI criteria detect complete responders with limited sensitivity because fibrosis, edema, and small foci of residual tumor can overlap after treatment. Radiomics and deep learning extract quantitative features beyond qualitative visual assessment. This narrative review examines their biological correlates and reported performance along the treatment pathway. We discuss tumor cellularity, fibrosis, spatial heterogeneity, segmentation, feature extraction, multimodal fusion, baseline prediction, longitudinal assessment, restaging, and recurrence risk. Previously published meta-analyses report summary areas under the curve of approximately 0.85 for MRI-based prediction of pathological complete response; these estimates were not pooled in this review and reflect heterogeneous imaging time points, response definitions, and validation methods. Representative studies are critically appraised using domains drawn from radiomics quality and prediction-model reporting frameworks. Most evidence remains retrospective, and external performance is variable. Imaging heterogeneity, post-treatment segmentation, limited numbers of complete responders, and inconsistent reference standards restrict applicability. Models trained on conventional chemoradiotherapy require evaluation in total neoadjuvant therapy and immunotherapy cohorts, while watch-and-wait models require sustained clinical complete response and local regrowth endpoints. Prospective observational validation should be distinguished from evaluation of model-guided care. Radiomics and deep learning remain investigational decision-support tools whose translation requires independent validation, calibrated risk estimates, workflow integration, and prospective evidence of clinical benefit.

Rethinking radiation dose optimization in pediatric computed tomography imaging: emerging algorithms and clinical integration.
articles.abstract: The optimization of radiation dose in pediatric computed tomography (CT) is a critical imperative, driven by the heightened radiosensitivity of children. This review provides a critical analysis of the evolution of dose optimization, from foundational principles like As Low As Reasonably Achievable (ALARA) and conventional techniques to the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI). We trace the progression from iterative reconstruction (IR), which offered initial dose reduction but was limited by unnatural image textures and computational demands, to the new paradigm of deep learning reconstruction (DLR) and emerging detector technologies like photon-counting CT. Clinical evidence demonstrates that DLR significantly shifts the traditional compromise between dose and image quality, enabling substantial potential dose reductions while producing images with superior noise properties and diagnostic confidence. Beyond reconstruction, AI is also automating scan protocoling to enhance consistency and reduce errors. However, the clinical integration of these powerful tools is not seamless. Significant barriers remain, including the "black box" nature of algorithms, the need for new training curricula for radiographers, and complex ethical and regulatory challenges. This review synthesizes these issues and charts a path forward, advocating for a holistic approach involving complementary AI-specific reference levels, federated learning, and robust governance to realize the full potential of a safer, more efficient, and patient-specific dose optimization ecosystem.

Evaluation Design and Reported Accuracy of Deep Learning Mandibular Canal Segmentation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Reported accuracy of deep learning mandibular canal segmentation varies widely, and studies differ in how it was evaluated. This systematic review estimated accuracy under explicit validity criteria and described how it varied with evaluation design. Five databases were searched to May 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261403406). Dice similarity coefficients (DSCs) from three-dimensional, patient-level-partitioned cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) or CT test sets were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. Public benchmark results were analyzed separately, and test sets whose reference was generated by the evaluated model were not pooled. Fifty-four studies were included. Pooled DSC across 15 studies was 0.826 (95% confidence interval 0.752-0.881; 95% prediction interval 0.444-0.966), close to three previous reviews with different inclusion rules (0.80-0.84). The 16 CBCT studies ineligible for pooling, mostly for two-dimensional slice-level segmentation or fewer than 10 test patients, reported a higher median DSC (0.860 versus 0.803). Two systems on the official ToothFairy test set had a pooled DSC of 0.751. Internal and external estimates did not differ significantly (P =  .974), but five external studies cannot establish equivalence. Pooled 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance across seven studies was 1.15 mm, with a prediction interval extending to 6.11 mm. Risk of bias was unclear or high in 14 of 15 pooled studies, and certainty of evidence was very low. Average accuracy is consistent across reviews, higher median values came, descriptively, from less constrained evaluations, and external evidence is too limited to show that performance transfers to new settings. Expert verification and prospective external validation remain necessary.

articles.title: Adnexal cyst pseudoenhancement and optimal attenuation change threshold determination at low keV reconstructions at photon counting CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate "pseudoenhancement" in adnexal lesions on low kiloelectron volt (keV) virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) at photon-counting CT (PCCT) and to establish optimal attenuation change thresholds for distinguishing enhancing from nonenhancing lesions at each VMI. METHODS: Adult women who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic PCCT and pelvic MRI or ultrasound (US) within 180 days were identified via retrospective PACS search. Adnexal lesions were classified as enhancing or nonenhancing using MRI or US as the reference standard. Quantitative attenuation measurements were obtained using regions-of-interest at VMI levels (70, 67, 60, 55, 50, 45, and 40 keV). "Pseudoenhancement" was defined as ≥ 20 Hounsfield units (HU) increase between the VMI and virtual unenhanced (VUE) images. The diagnostic performance of a 20HU change to define enhancement at each VMI level was assessed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine optimal thresholds by maximizing the Youden index. Inter-reader agreement was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients. RESULTS: Forty-five women (median [IQR] age 46 years [37, 54] ) with 30 nonenhancing and 15 enhancing adnexal lesions were included. No "pseudoenhancement" was observed at 70 or 67 keV; however, "pseudoenhancement" was observed in 3.3% of patients at 60 keV, increasing to 26.7% at 40 keV. Using a 20 HU change to indicate enhancement had 47% sensitivity with 100% specificity at 70 keV and 93% sensitivity with 73% specificity at 40 keV. Optimal attenuation thresholds increased with decreasing energy, from 10.0 HU at 70 keV to 36.3 HU at 40 keV. Notably, at 60 keV, the threshold was 19.1HU. Inter-reader agreement was near perfect (ICC = 0.858, 95%CI = 0.756-0.920). CONCLUSION: "Pseudoenhancement" of adnexal lesions occurs with increasing frequency with decreasing keV below 60 keV, but there was no "pseudoenhancement" at 67 or 70 keV. Energy-specific attenuation thresholds improve adnexal lesion characterization.

articles.title: FOCUS: A Frequency Offset Selection Framework for Accelerated CEST MRI Using Adaptive Subset-Level Optimization.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a redundancy-aware frequency offset selection framework for accelerated chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) MRI that reduces acquired saturation frequency offsets while preserving quantitative and classification performance. METHODS: FOCUS, a Frequency Offset selection framework for accelerated CEST MRI Using adaptive Subset-level optimization, was developed to account for inter-offset redundancy beyond individual offset importance. Frequency offset selection was formulated as subset-level optimization, in which candidate subsets were encoded as binary individuals and evaluated by final task performance. An artificial protozoa optimizer-based search scheme was used to explore the subset space, and a deep Q-network adaptively guided the search strategy. FOCUS was evaluated in numerical simulations, in vivo human skeletal muscle phosphocreatine quantification, and glioma molecular subtype classification, and compared with permutation importance analysis, random forest, and channel pruning. RESULTS: Under reduced frequency-offset sampling, FOCUS outperformed existing methods in both CEST quantification and glioma molecular subtype classification. For CEST quantification, FOCUS achieved the lowest root mean square error in simulations and in vivo skeletal muscle experiments, with the highest structural similarity index and peak signal-to-noise ratio in vivo. For glioma classification, FOCUS achieved the best overall performance in predicting isocitrate dehydrogenase mutation and O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation status. CONCLUSION: FOCUS enables redundancy-aware frequency offset selection for accelerated CEST MRI, reducing acquired saturation frequency offsets while preserving quantitative accuracy and classification performance.

articles.title: Region-Adaptive White Matter Tractography Using Microstructure-Informed Diffusion Metrics.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate a region-adaptive tractography framework that integrates multi-scale diffusion metrics, specifically fractional anisotropy (FA), asymmetric index (ASI) from asymmetric fiber orientation distribution functions, and diffusion tensor distribution (DTD)-derived microscopic fractional anisotropy (μFA) to improve anatomical fidelity in complex white matter configurations. METHODS: MS-Track, a rule-based region-adaptive tractography method, was proposed to classify local fiber configurations (parallel, crossing, bending, termination) using FA, ASI, and μFA. Streamline seeding, peak sampling, curvature tolerance, and termination were dynamically modulated according to configuration. Validation was performed on the ISMRM 2015 Tractography Challenge phantom and in vivo data acquired with the DTD protocol from 20 healthy subjects, 20 arteriovenous malformation (AVM) patients, and 2 glioma patients. RESULTS: On the ISMRM 2015 Challenge dataset, a mean Dice coefficient of 0.700 was achieved by MS-Track, with the highest overlap (68.5%) and the lowest overreach (24.0%) among state-of-the-art methods. In AVM patients, reduced fiber density and elevated μFA and ASI were observed in affected tracts. In glioma cases, μFA increased with tumor grade, consistent with histological findings. CONCLUSION: Tractography reliability in complex white matter was improved by MS-Track through the integration of complementary microstructural contrasts. DTD-derived μFA provided additional sensitivity to pathological tissue, supporting potential clinical translation in surgical planning and disease characterization.

articles.title: The 3‑mm peritumoral margin provides optimal prognostic information in soft tissue sarcoma radiomics: a retrospective multi‑sequence MRI study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To construct an integrated prognostic model combining intra‑ and peritumoral radiomics with MRI features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in soft tissue sarcomas (STS). METHODS: This retrospective study included 305 patients with trunk or extremity STS. Radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and peritumoral regions at expansion distances of 3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm on both contrast‑enhanced T1‑weighted (CE‑T1WI) and fat‑suppressed T2‑weighted (FS‑T2WI) sequences. Features were selected via ICC, univariate Cox, and LASSO Cox regression. Prognostic models were constructed by integrating Rad‑scores with significant MRI features, and evaluated using C‑index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed stratified by imaging phenotype (cellular vs. non‑cellular). Correlation analyses between peritumoral Rad‑scores and semantic MRI features were also conducted. RESULTS: The 3‑mm peritumoral expansion yielded the highest predictive performance among the three distances. Integrated intratumoral-peritumoral (3 mm) models from both sequences outperformed single‑region models. The 3‑mm margin consistently demonstrated superior performance in both cellular and non‑cellular phenotypes. The final multimodal model, combining dual‑sequence Rad‑scores with peritumoral enhancement, achieved a C‑index of 0.888 in the validation set. Correlation analyses reveal that peritumoral Rad‑scores are most strongly associated with peritumoral T2 hyperintensity, with differential correlation patterns between CE‑T1WI and FS‑T2WI supporting their complementary roles. CONCLUSIONS: We developed a robust multimodal radiomics model integrating intra‑ and peritumoral (3 mm) features with key MRI characteristics. The optimality of the 3‑mm margin was validated across major STS phenotypes. This non‑invasive tool facilitates personalized risk stratification and may inform adjuvant treatment decisions, supporting clinical translation in STS management.

articles.title: Best of Times, Worst of Times: State Economic Conditions and Medicare Imaging Composition Across Two Macroeconomic Episodes.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the determinants of imaging utilization across two distinct macroeconomic disruptions by comparing the elective musculoskeletal (MSK) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-urgent computed tomography (CT) ratio during the Great Recession recovery and the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. MATERIALS AND METHODS: State-level utilization data for elective MSK MRI and urgent CT codes were obtained from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Physician and Other Practitioners by Geography and Service Public Use Files (2013-2023), state annual unemployment rates from the Bureau of Labor Statistics Local Area Unemployment Statistics program, and diagnostic radiologist density per 100,000 population from a published aggregation of the National Provider Identifier registry. Associations between changes in the elective-to-urgent imaging ratio and state unemployment were evaluated across both periods. Multivariable linear regression assessed the contributions of unemployment change and diagnostic radiologist density. RESULTS: During the Great Recession recovery, larger declines in unemployment were associated with greater increases in the elective-to-urgent imaging ratio (r = -0.36, p = 0.010). Each 1% decrease in unemployment corresponded to approximately 8 additional elective MSK MRI examinations per 1000 urgent CT examinations (β = -7.85, 95% CI -13.76--1.94). No such association was observed during the COVID-19 period (r = 0.07, p = 0.61). In multivariable analysis, unemployment change predicted imaging composition during the recession recovery, whereas diagnostic radiologist density approached significance as a negative predictor during COVID-19 (β = -3.05, p = 0.05). On cross-sectional analysis, elective-to-urgent imaging ratio varied 2.4-fold across states, remained stable over time (r = 0.80-0.88), and was inversely associated with radiologist density (r = -0.32--0.44). CONCLUSION: Imaging composition reflected demand-side economic recovery after the Great Recession but was more closely associated with supply-side constraints during the COVID-19 pandemic, suggesting that the effects of macroeconomic conditions on imaging utilization depend on the nature of the underlying shock.

articles.title: Static and Dynamic Functional Connectivity Alterations of Medial and Lateral Entorhinal Cortex with Subjective Cognitive Decline.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Entorhinal cortex (EC), which is vulnerable in Alzheimer's disease (AD), comprises the medial (MEC) and lateral (LEC) regions encoding spatial navigation and olfactory information, respectively. However, it remains unclear whether static functional connectivity (sFC) and dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) of MEC and LEC are altered in subjective cognitive decline (SCD), a preclinical stage of AD, and how these changes relate to these functions. This study aims to explore the alterations in the sFC and dFC of LEC and MEC with the whole brain in the SCD population, and further to assess the relationships of these connectivity changes with olfactory and spatial navigation functions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted neuropsychological evaluations, resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging, spatial navigation, and olfactory assessment in 77 healthy controls (HCs) and 106 individuals with SCD. Bilateral MEC and LEC were defined as separate seed regions to calculate their sFC and dFC with all other voxels in the brain. Nested cross-validation classification analysis was applied to evaluate the classification efficacy for distinguishing SCD from HC. RESULTS: SCD individuals exhibited decreased sFC between MEC/LEC and widespread brain regions, primarily within the visual, sensory motor, and default mode network. The dFC between the left MEC and right putamen, and between the right MEC and right middle temporal gyrus increased, while decreased dFC was observed between the right LEC and right triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus. The connectivity between the LEC and visual network was significantly correlated with the olfactory recognition function. The predictive model combining sFC and dFC features from bilateral MEC and LEC achieved an area under the curve of 0.863. CONCLUSION: This study revealed that sFC and dFC alterations of MEC/LEC have occurred at the SCD stage, and these changes are correlated with spatial navigation and olfactory performance, demonstrating their potential as biomarkers for identifying individuals at risk for AD.

articles.title: Cross validation of Ultrasound- and Serum-Based Scores for Fibrosis Assessment after Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to conduct a comprehensive comparison of non-invasive diagnostic approaches for graft fibrosis (shear wave elastography (SWE), serum-based scores) in liver transplant (LT) recipients against transient elastography (TE). Materials & Methods In this retrospective analysis of 195 liver transplant recipients from a tertiary transplant center, an ultrasound-based technique (SWE PLUS) and serum-based scores were compared with TE. Liver stiffness > 7.5 kPa was defined as significant fibrosis. All data were collected at one visit and ultrasound measurements followed FESUMB guidelines. Statistics included correlation analysis, uni- and multivariable logistic regression and AUROC analyses. DeLong test was used to compare AUCs. Results Median time from LT were 49 months with 44 % females and a median age of 59 years. SWE PLUS showed a strong correlation with TE (rho = 0.69, p < 0.0001) and an excellent diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.901. In univariable regression analysis, the serum-based scores were associated with the presence of significant fibrosis. In multivariable analysis only SWE PLUS was an independent predictor of significant fibrosis (OR = 2.561, p < 0.001). SWE PLUS outperformed all serum-based tests for the detection of graft fibrosis (each p < 0.001). Conclusion Our results demonstrate applicability of SWE for the diagnosis of graft fibrosis in LT recipients. SWE PLUS may represent a promising alternative to TE for graft fibrosis detection. Materialien & Methoden In dieser retrospektiven Analyse von 195 Lebertransplantierten wurden SWE PLUS sowie serumbasierte Scores mit transienter Elastographie verglichen. Eine Lebersteifigkeit > 7,5 kPa definierte eine signifikante Transplantatfibrose. Alle Daten wurden im Rahmen eines einzelnen Untersuchungstermins erhoben; die Ultraschallmessungen erfolgten gemäß den EFSUMB-Leitlinien. Die Analysen umfassten Korrelationsanalysen, uni- und multivariable logistische Regressionsanalysen sowie AUROC-Analysen und den Vergleich der AUROCs mittels DeLong-Test. SWE PLUS korrelierte stark mit TE (rho = 0,69; p < 0,0001) und zeigte eine AUC von 0,901. SWE PLUS zeigte sich signifikant besser in der Prädiktion der Transplantatfibrose verglichen mit allen untersuchten serumbasierten Scores (p jeweils < 0.001).
