SWE PLUS stellt eine vielversprechende Alternative zur TE für die Detektion einer Transplantatfibrose dar.

articles.title: Radiomics-Based Prediction of Post-TACE Milan Criteria Status and Survival Outcomes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Retrospective Machine Learning Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate machine learning models integrating radiomic features from pre- and post-transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) CT and MRI with clinical variables to predict 6-month Milan criteria status, overall survival (OS), and time to progression (TTP) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 428 treatment-naive patients with biopsy-confirmed HCC who underwent conventional TACE (2010-2025) with post-TACE CT, pre- and post-TACE MRI, and 6-month imaging follow-up. nnU-Net segmented CT (liver, lipiodol, tumor) and MRI (liver, tumor) compartments, and radiomic features were extracted. Five feature configurations (shape and first-order features, alone and with clinical variables, and both combined with clinical variables) were evaluated. AutoGluon predicted 6-month Milan status, evaluated by repeated 5×5 cross-validation (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]) and compared with clinical-only and baseline-Milan reference models; OS and TTP were assessed by concordance index (C-index) with leakage-corrected repeated cross-validation. RESULTS: Cross-validated Milan AUCs were 0.766-0.791 for radiomic configurations, exceeding a clinical-only model (0.711) but not baseline Milan status alone (0.842); adding shape features to clinical variables and baseline Milan status did not improve discrimination (0.874 vs 0.865; P = .43). Shape features with clinical variables had the numerically highest C-index for OS (0.647) and TTP (0.571), without improvement over clinical-only models. CONCLUSION: Shape descriptors carried most of the imaging signal for 6-month Milan status, adding discrimination beyond clinical variables but not beyond baseline Milan status; survival discrimination was modest (OS) to near chance (TTP).

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Percutaneous Sclerotherapy using Sodium Tetradecyl Sulfate for the Primary Management of Aneurysmal Bone Cysts.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the clinical and radiological effectiveness and safety of using sodium tetradecyl sulfate (STS) during percutaneous sclerotherapy for the primary treatment of aneurysmal bone cysts (ABCs). MATERIALS AND METHODS: - A retrospective data search from December 2015 to August 2023 included 23 patients with histologically proven ABCs who underwent sclerotherapy as primary management. Pre- and post- sclerotherapy imaging was obtained with images anonymized and randomized for evaluation of tumor volume and appearances as per the Royal Orthopedic Hospital scoring system. Evaluation of clinical response was determined through clinic letters. RESULTS: -There were no immediate adverse events following sclerotherapy with STS. The Pearson correlation for inter-observer agreement of radiological tumor assessment by two independent reviewers was strongly positive (p= <0.05). Over 50% tumor volume reduction was noted in 4 cases, >25%- 50% tumor volume reduction in 5 cases and failed tumor volume reduction in 10 cases. Using the ROH scoring system for radiological success, 5 cases had excellent success, 4 cases had a good outcome, 3 equivocal and 7 had a poor outcome. 71% of patients reported improved ability to carry out daily activities. All spinal ABCs had positive radiological and clinical outcomes. Surgery was not required for any of the ABCs located in the spine or sacrum. CONCLUSION: Sclerotherapy using STS is an effective and safe first-line treatment method for ABCs, particularly in the spine, where it can be used as the primary treatment method and have the potential to avoid the requirement for surgery and neurological deficit.

articles.title: Variceal Embolization Combined With Partial Splenic Embolization for Recurrent Variceal Bleeding in Cavernous Transformation of the Portal Vein: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of variceal embolization (VE) combined with partial splenic embolization (PSE) for recurrent variceal bleeding in patients with cavernous transformation of the portal vein (CTPV) who were not candidates for transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with CTPV and recurrent gastroesophageal variceal bleeding who underwent VE plus PSE between January 2020 and August 2024. The primary effectiveness endpoint was variceal rebleeding. Secondary endpoints included non-variceal rebleeding, new or worsening ascites, overt hepatic encephalopathy, changes in liver function, and survival time. Safety was assessed by procedure-related complications. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to evaluate variceal rebleeding and survival. RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included, all had noncirrhotic CTPV (100%). Median follow-up was 825 days. Ten patients (43.5%) presented with acute bleeding; bleeding was controlled in all (immediate hemostasis rate, 100%). During follow-up, 11 patients (47.8%) experienced variceal rebleeding, with a median time to rebleeding of 217 days. New or worsening ascites occurred in 2 patients (8.7%). Two patients (8.7%) died. Liver function remained stable, with a significant increase in albumin levels at 1 year (P = .032). No major procedure-related complications were observed. CONCLUSIONS: VE combined with PSE was feasible and demonstrated an acceptable safety profile in patients with CTPV and recurrent variceal bleeding who were not candidates for TIPS, and it may represent a treatment option in selected high-risk patients.

articles.title: Evolving Embolization Strategy for Congenital Renal Arteriovenous Malformations from Feeder-Oriented to Venous-Oriented Approaches: A 15-Year Single-Center Outcome Analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate embolization outcomes for congenital renal arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) and the impact of an evolving angiographic classification-guided strategy on renal parenchymal preservation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 29 patients (33 sessions; 25 women; mean age, 52.0 ± 11.8 years) treated between 2010 and 2025. AVMs were categorized according to Do's angiographic classification. For type I AVMs, treatment transitioned from transarterial coils to through-and-through vascular plug embolization. For type IIIb AVMs, selective feeder angiography identified common venous targets for transvenous embolization. RESULTS: AVMs comprised type I (n = 8), type II (n =10), and type IIIb (n =11). Complete devascularization was achieved in 25 patients (86.2%) after one session and all 29 after a second session, yielding 100% final technical success. Clinical success was achieved in all 28 patients with available clinical follow-up (100%), with no recurrence over a mean of 23.9 months. Renal parenchymal infarction occurred in 18 of 20 sessions (90.0%) involving transarterial access (TA alone or TA+TV; mean infarcted area, 22.7%; range, 5-50%) versus none after transvenous, direct percutaenous, or through-and-through approaches. All 4 type I AVMs treated with the through-and-through vascular plug embolization were occluded without infarction. Overall renal function remained stable. Mild adverse events (SIR grade 1) occurred in 5 patients (17.2%), with no adverse events of SIR grade 2 or higher. CONCLUSIONS: Classification-guided selection of embolization strategies based on AVM architecture and venous anatomy may reduce renal parenchymal injury while preserving treatment efficacy.

articles.title: Interpretable MEG decoding of perceived speech: Source-space patterns and the stimulus features that drive retrieval.
articles.abstract: Short segments of perceived speech can be retrieved from non-invasive magnetoencephalographic (MEG) recordings by a deep network trained with a CLIP-style objective against wav2vec 2.0 audio embeddings (Défossez et al., 2023; Baevski et al., 2020; Radford et al., 2021). Such studies do not convert their weights into the notions used in classical electrophysiology. Although the spatial filters in the front end of Défossez et al. (2023) could in principle be mapped to source topographies, the dynamic properties of those sources remain out of reach. Which properties of the speech stream contribute to the decoding is equally unclear. Here we scrutinize a decoder with a physiologically motivated, factorized spatial-temporal front end that permits joint interpretation of learned spatial topographies and temporal patterns in relation to the MEG forward model. Building on the framework of Petrosyan et al. (2021, 2022), we replace the 2D Fourier spatial attention of Défossez et al. (2023) with a layer parameterized by spherical harmonics (Sivakumar et al., 2016), reduce the subject-specific representation from 270 to K=25 branches, and add trainable temporal filters so that each branch has an explicit learned spatial filter and temporal response. Ocular and cardiac components are removed before training, since either could supply stimulus-locked information that would otherwise be mistaken for cortical. On the cleaned MEG-MASC dataset (Gwilliams et al., 2023) the model reaches 39.75±0.34% Top-1 accuracy among 1005 candidates across six model initializations (mean ± SD), with approximately 20× fewer trainable parameters in the decoder. Its learned spatial patterns can be mapped through a cortical inverse model (Petrosyan et al., 2021; Haufe et al., 2014), yielding approximate source-magnitude projections with recurrent bilateral structure over lateral cortex, concentrated around temporal and adjacent peri-Sylvian regions. Paired MEG occlusion, replacing feature-marked speech segments with matched donors from feature-present and feature-absent intervals, shows significant positive effects for 15 of 19 tested stimulus features, the largest effects being silence, sound intensity, vowels and acoustic onsets. Intriguingly, the randomly ordered word lists behave oppositely: replacing word-list MEG with MEG recorded during coherent narrative improves retrieval relative to word-list donor MEG. The wav2vec target can be reduced to about twelve learned feature dimensions with only a small reduction in retrieval accuracy, whereas strong temporal compression causes a clear performance loss. Decoders with physiologically interpretable spatial-temporal front ends can thus serve as knowledge-discovery tools: their learned weights can be converted into source-space and temporal patterns, while input interventions reveal what the decision rule relies on.

articles.title: NUCLEON: An Ontology of Chemical Elements and Nuclides for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Nuclear Medicine.
articles.abstract: Radiopharmaceutical information in imaging systems is typically recorded as free text or as flat code system entries that include little or no computable information about radionuclides' physical properties. This article introduces the Nuclide and Element Ontology (NUCLEON), a machine-processable knowledge resource that represents the 118 known chemical elements and 5408 nuclides, including 2019 metastable isomers, with computable nuclear properties. The ontology declares each element and nuclide as both a class and an individual: the class structure generates a taxonomy that aligns with vocabularies of chemistry and clinical medicine, and the individual entities support quantitative assertions, such as half-life. Each of 7691 decay branches is an individual specifying its mode of decay and branching ratio; 7399 branches have an explicit link to their decay product (daughter) nuclide, derived from the decay mode rather than transcribed. Ground-state data were taken from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) LiveChart of Nuclides, isomer data from the NUBASE2020 evaluation, and the energies and yields of 3990 radiation emissions of clinically coded radionuclides and their decay chains from International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) Publication 107; symbols and names were verified against standard chemical nomenclature. NUCLEON is linked to the Ontology of Chemical Elements, SNOMED Clinical Terms, and DICOM radiopharmaceutical isotope and PET radionuclide code sequences, allowing a nuclide to be resolved directly from a DICOM header. The ontology incorporates 215,862 triples across 5533 classes and 17,253 named individuals. Automated checks confirmed the arithmetic consistency of atomic, neutron, and mass numbers, and none of the derived decay products disagreed with ICRP Publication 107 or the Evaluated Nuclear Structure Data File. Element names are provided in seven languages. NUCLEON is available at https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/NUCLEON .

articles.title: Transducin: An Open-Source Pipeline Recovering SNOMED-CT Coded Measurements from the Undocumented Optopol .OPT and Zeiss Cirrus Private-Tag Formats as DICOM Structured Reports.
articles.abstract: Quantitative optical coherence tomography (OCT) measurements are essential for retinal disease monitoring, yet leading vendors store acquisition data in undocumented proprietary formats or encode measurements exclusively in private DICOM tags inaccessible to open systems, obstructing interoperability between devices and standards-based clinical imaging infrastructure. We present Transducin, an open-source Python library that reverse-engineers two undocumented proprietary OCT formats (the Optopol REVO FC130/REVO 60 .OPT binary format and the Zeiss Cirrus HD-OCT 500 private DICOM tags) through systematic binary analysis cross-referenced against DICOM-exported metadata from the same studies, and converts the recovered measurements into standard, vendor-neutral DICOM TID 1500 Structured Reports with SNOMED-CT coded findings. Format stability was validated across SOCT software versions 11.5.0-21.5.0, spanning approximately 8 years of development; a laterality-inference hypothesis derived from the device's scan-geometry parameters was tested against known eye assignment; and all generated DICOM objects were checked against pydicom's conformance validator and ingested into a clinical PACS. The validation corpus comprised 475 Optopol .OPT files across two clinical sites: 387 at Site A (Chihuahua; 73 patients) and 88 at Site B (Querétaro), spanning three device models and four SOCT software versions with 100% parse success across nine acquisition types. The Zeiss Cirrus pipeline generated TID 1500 SRs for all 41 applicable studies (100%), yielding CMT 203-630 µm and RNFL 53-123 µm across a clinically representative range. A scan-geometry parameter recorded by the device (OCTPARAMS tag 23, the horizontal position of the foveal or disc reflex relative to scan center) was found to encode ocular laterality through its arithmetic sign-an anatomical consequence of the fovea's nasal position relative to the optic disc-and this laterality-inference method was validated across 18 files from two device models and two software versions with 100% accuracy, requiring no operator data entry or filename convention. Transducin provides the first publicly documented specification of the Optopol .OPT format and the first open-source multivendor pipeline generating SNOMED-CT coded DICOM Structured Reports from both Optopol REVO and Zeiss Cirrus devices, closing a gap explicitly confirmed by both manufacturers' own documentation and final users experience. The code is available at https://github.com/oftalmos-org/transducin (Apache License 2.0).

articles.title: Native-Resolution Cascaded Refinement Improves Reliability of Automated Landmark Localization on Full-Length Lower-Limb Radiographs.
articles.abstract: To assess whether native-resolution cascaded refinement improves the reliability of automated lower-limb landmark localization beyond mean error. This retrospective study included 965 full-length lower-limb radiographs from distinct Osteoarthritis Initiative participants (675 training, 144 validation, 146 internal evaluation). Sixteen landmarks were localized by 512 × 512 heatmap regression and refined within 256 × 256 native-resolution regions. Analyses covered landmark-specific errors, alignment measurements, cross-dataset and prosthesis stress tests, image perturbations, and failure recognition using 12 inference-only features. Paired bootstrap intervals retained within-radiograph clustering. Evaluation used reference-informed image preparation and documented image-coordinate scales. Refinement reduced mean radial error from 2.433 to 1.987 image-grid mm. Cases with mean error greater than 3 mm decreased from 13.0% (19/146) to 3.4% (5/146), and landmarks within 3 mm increased from 71.5% (1671/2336) to 80.4% (1877/2336). Lateral femoral condyles accounted for 40/106 residual landmark errors above 5 mm. Mean absolute mechanical lateral distal femoral and medial proximal tibial angle errors decreased by 0.620° and 0.276°, respectively; change intervals for hip-knee-ankle angle and mechanical axis deviation included zero. The risk model improved failure ranking during validation but did not outperform ensemble disagreement on internal evaluation. Native-resolution cascaded refinement improved tail reliability, with measurement benefits concentrated in joint-orientation angles. Inference-time features did not provide a generalizable failure-warning mechanism.

articles.title: Different diffusion priors and their ensemble for sparse-view CT reconstruction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for medical image reconstruction, but their use requires careful balancing between data fidelity and learned diffusion priors. This study proposes an ensemble-based sparse-view CT reconstruction method that automatically optimizes this trade-off. METHODS: We develop an ensemble framework that combines reconstructions obtained from multiple time steps of a pre-trained denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM), corresponding to different noise levels. Reconstructions at small time steps emphasize measurement consistency and preserve fine anatomical details but tend to retain artifacts, whereas those at large time steps rely more strongly on the diffusion prior, reducing artifacts at the expense of structural fidelity. The proposed method integrates these complementary reconstructions using spatially adaptive weights optimized during reconstruction. RESULTS: Experiments on sparse-view CT reconstruction show that the proposed ensemble approach effectively reduces artifacts while preserving anatomical structures in moderately sparse acquisition settings. Quantitative evaluations using SSIM and PSNR demonstrate improved performance compared with iterative reconstruction (IR), IR with total variation regularization (IR+TV), diffusion posterior sampling (DPS), and decomposed diffusion sampler (DDS). However, in extremely sparse conditions (e.g., 25 views), the advantage of the ensemble becomes limited due to severe information loss. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework enables effective balancing of data fidelity and diffusion priors in sparse-view CT reconstruction when a moderate level of measurement information is available. By leveraging complementary information across different diffusion priors, the method improves reconstruction quality and structural consistency, indicating potential utility for radiation dose reduction in CT imaging.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Comparative predictive value of modified CT-PCI and PET-PCI for surgical resectability and overall survival in pseudomyxoma peritonei.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate total and selected (regions 2 and 9-12) CT‑based and PET‑based Peritoneal Cancer Index (CT‑PCI and PET‑PCI) for predicting surgical resectability and overall survival (OS) in pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP). METHODS: 54 patients were retrospectively enrolled. The predictive performance of total and selected CT-PCI and PET-PCI for surgical resectability was assessed using ROC curve analysis. OS was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, with comparisons stratified by CT-PCI, PET-PCI, and completeness of cytoreduction (CCR) scores. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent prognostic factors. RESULTS: CT-PCI demonstrated high predictive accuracy for resectability (total: 92.6%; selected: 90.7%), whereas PET-PCI showed moderate to high accuracy (total: 74.1%; selected: 88.8%). Patients with high total or selected CT-PCI or PET-PCI scores had worse OS than those with low scores (all log-rank P < 0.001). Significant OS differences were also observed between CCR subgroups: CCR 0-1 versus CCR 3 (P = 0.04), CCR 0-1 versus CCR 4 (P < 0.001), and CCR 2 versus CCR 4 (P = 0.011). Notably, OS didn't differ significantly between CCR 3 (incomplete cytoreduction) and CCR 4 (no surgery). Multivariate Cox regression identified both CT-PCI (HR = 5.589, P = 0.033) and PET-PCI (HR = 6.992, P = 0.007) as independent prognostic factors for OS. CONCLUSION: Both total and selected CT-PCI and PET-PCI are useful for predicting resectability and OS in PMP patients. CT-PCI is more suitable for preoperative resectability assessment, whereas PET-PCI provides complementary prognostic information. Selected PCI (regions 2 and 9-12) showed predictive performance comparable to that of total PCI while requiring assessment of fewer regions.

articles.title: Development and temporal validation of a bedside score for acute occlusive mesenteric ischemia in emergency mesenteric CTA candidates: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and temporally validate a bedside risk score (BTCH-AOMI) based exclusively on pre-CTA clinical variables to predict acute occlusive mesenteric ischemia (AOMI) in emergency CTA-selected patients. METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 285 adult patients (development cohort [2017-2022]: n = 187, 85 AOMI; temporal validation cohort [2023-2024]: n = 98, 42 AOMI). A 0-5-point score was constructed using four pre-CTA predictors: abdominal distension (1 point), AOMI risk conditions (1 point), peritonitis (2 points), and bedside inflammatory response (1 point). Score performance was evaluated and compared with an operationalized "pain-out-of-proportion" rule. RESULTS: In temporal validation, the BTCH-AOMI score achieved moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.744, 95% CI: 0.651-0.834), significantly outperforming the pain-out-of-proportion rule (AUC: 0.521, 95% CI: 0.441-0.601; P = 0.002). Observed AOMI rates across validation strata (0-1, 2-3, and 4-5 points) were 25.0%, 45.5%, and 88.2%, respectively. A threshold of ≥ 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 71.4% and specificity of 64.3%; a threshold of ≥ 1 point yielded 95.2% sensitivity and 23.2% specificity. CONCLUSIONS: The BTCH-AOMI score demonstrates moderate temporal discrimination and superior performance over traditional "pain-out-of-proportion" assessment. It is intended strictly as an adjunct for risk stratification and prioritization within emergency CTA pathways, not as a tool to exclude AOMI or replace CTA imaging.

articles.title: Use of a large language model for identification and extraction of actionable details from recommendations for additional imaging in abdominopelvic CT reports.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Automated identification and extraction of recommendations for additional imaging (RAI) from radiology reports could facilitate closed-loop tracking and follow-up completion. We compare a prompt-engineered GPT-4.1 large language model (LLM) versus a validated encoder-only transformer deep learning model (bidirectional encoder representations from transformers [BERT]) for detection of RAI in abdominopelvic computed tomography (CTAP) reports, and evaluate GPT-4.1 for extraction of actionable RAI elements. METHODS: This retrospective study included CTAP reports from a multi-institution system in 2023. LLM and BERT were used to identify RAI from radiology reports; LLM also extracted RAI actionable elements (modality, body part, time frame, rationale). Recall, precision, F1, and accuracy for RAI detection were determined using human-annotated reference standard. Paired comparison between each model's accuracy used McNemar's test. LLM recall, precision, F1, and accuracy for actionable element extraction were computed. Element prevalence was compared using chi-square test. RESULTS: 2000 random reports for unique patients (58% women; mean age 58.5 ± 17.5) included 215 RAI within 206 reports. For RAI detection, GPT-4.1 recall, precision, F1 and accuracy were 95.6%, 98.5%, 97.0% and 99.4%, respectively; BERT recall, precision, F1 and accuracy were 93.7%, 96.5%, 95.1% and 99.0% (p = 0.16). Recommendation element recall were as follows: 100.0% for time frame, 93.9% for body part, 90.2% for rationale, and 94.2% for modality. Precision were 100.0%, 95.7%, 94.6% and 86.1%, respectively. 29/215 (13.5%) RAI were complete (specified all actionable elements). Prevalence of actionable elements varied (p < 0.001), highest for rationale (215/215, 100%), followed by body part (213/215, 99.1%), modality (191/215, 88.8%), and time frame (31/215, 14.4%). CONCLUSION: GPT-4.1 demonstrated high accuracy for extraction of RAI and enabled accurate extraction of actionable elements. LLM integration into radiology workflows can facilitate automatic closed-loop communication and tracking of recommended imaging, which may reduce diagnostic delays.

articles.title: Drawing the line: tumour contact length in the VI-RADS grey zone.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether tumour contact length improves discrimination of muscle-invasive bladder cancer within Vesical Imaging-Reporting and Data System (VI-RADS) categories 2 and 3 on 3.0 T multiparametric MRI. METHODS: This prospective single-centre study included 207 consecutive adults with a bladder mass who underwent 3.0 T multiparametric MRI before transurethral resection between February 2024 and January 2026. Two radiologists, blinded to histopathology, independently assigned VI-RADS categories and measured contact length. Histopathology of the resection specimen, or of re-resection when detrusor muscle was absent, was the reference standard. The primary analysis compared contact length ≥ 30 mm with VI-RADS 3 versus 2 within the VI-RADS 2-3 subgroup using McNemar's exact test. RESULTS: Ninety-two patients (44.4%) had muscle-invasive disease. Within the VI-RADS 2-3 subgroup (n = 101; 24 muscle-invasive), contact length ≥ 30 mm yielded a sensitivity of 87.5% (95% CI 67.6-97.3) and a specificity of 76.6% (65.6-85.5), compared with 79.2% and 62.3% for VI-RADS 3 versus 2 (McNemar p = 0.69 and p = 0.043, respectively). Muscle invasion was present in 10.0% of VI-RADS 3 lesions below 30 mm and 60.7% at or above it; for VI-RADS 2 lesions, the proportions were 2.4% and 36.4%. Requiring both criteria increased specificity to 85.7% but missed 7 of 24 muscle-invasive tumours. Inter-reader agreement for contact length was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.906). CONCLUSION: Within VI-RADS 2-3, a pre-specified 30 mm contact-length threshold improved specificity without a significant difference in sensitivity and was reproducible. Contact length complements the VI-RADS category and requires prospective multicentre validation.

articles.title: A closer look at magnetic field corrections for a 0.35 T MRI-Linac.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Magnetic FIeld COrrection (FICO) was implemented on a 0.35 T MRI-Linac to minimize B0 off-resonances. FICO parameters were derived from phantom measurements conducted at 30° gantry angle increments. FICO data were interpolated for every gantry angle, stored in a look-up table, and read during MRI-Linac simulation and treatment. PURPOSE: Verify the performance and efficacy of FICO. METHODS: We measured off-resonances in a 24 cm diameter spherical volume phantom and compared the FICO values to our measurements conducted at every: (1) gantry angle for center frequency and gradient shim; (2) 2° increment for B0 eddy currents; and (3) 10° increment for gradient and cross-term eddy currents. FICO results were compared with pre-FICO methods using the settings from a single home gantry angle (HGA), for example, 300°. RESULTS: Off-resonances decreased from a mean of -20.19 (HGA) to -0.61 Hz (FICO). Dispersion decreased from 81.10 Hz (HGA) to 52.71 Hz (FICO) and 28.0 Hz (FICO with gradient shim updates). B0 eddy currents remained within specification (± 0.1 µT∙m/mT) with FICO. X-B0 and Y-B0 eddy currents exceeded the limit when using HGA. Gradient and cross-term eddy currents were within limits (± 0.1%) for both FICO and HGA. X and cross-term (Y→X, and X→Z) eddy currents were significantly smaller with FICO than with HGA (p ≤ 0.02). Gradient eddy currents generally dropped by 24% using FICO versus HGA. X and Y gradient shim root mean square errors dropped by half by reducing the gantry angle increment from 30° to 20°. CONCLUSIONS: FICO resulted in reductions in center frequency offsets and full width at half maximum (FWHM) values, gradient shim amplitudes, and B0 eddy currents. Therefore, FICO is beneficial for minimizing off-resonances. However, FICO will benefit from using smaller gantry angle increments for interpolations and updating the gradient shim amplitudes and center frequency offsets before each treatment gantry angle.

articles.title: A multi-resolution SWIN transformer framework regularized by white matter time-intensity curve for brain dynamic contrast-enhanced MR image registration.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep learning-based registration methods are often computationally intensive and struggle with dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) images, as they cannot effectively distinguish motion artifacts from contrast-induced intensity variations, leading to unreliable physiological parameter estimation. PURPOSE: To develop a novel registration framework (TIC-SViT) based on a multi-resolution SWIN transformer architecture that exploits the inherent smoothness of tissue time-intensity curves (TICs). METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on DCE-MRI brain data from 59 subjects, acquired using a 3.0 T scanner with a T1-weighted spoiled gradient echo sequence. The dataset was randomly split into training (n = 4956), validation (n = 1180), and testing (n = 59) pairs. Model performance was assessed in terms of computational efficiency, registration accuracy, and clinical relevance. Comparative experiments were conducted against four representative registration approaches: the traditional optimization-based method ANTs, a CNN-based deep learning model, the groupwise multi-resolution framework (GWMS), and the transformer-based C2FViT framework. Computational efficiency was assessed by comparing parameter count, training time, and testing time per DCE-MRI case. Registration accuracy was quantified using Dice coefficient (DC) and the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) across white matter, gray matter, and cerebrospinal fluid. In addition, the temporal smoothness of TICs in arterial, venous, and white matter regions was evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE). Clinical relevance was examined by comparing the quality of DCE-derived parameter maps generated from different registration methods. RESULTS: The proposed TIC-SViT model achieved a comparable parameter count (12.2 M, compared with 11.7, 9.5, and 12.4 M for CNN, GWMS, and C2FViT, respectively), the shortest training time and competitive testing speed (775 s and 11.7 s per case, compared with 1142 and 52.6 s for CNN, 1440 and 8.9 s for GWMS, 857 and 39.4 s for C2FViT, and 159.3 s for ANTs, which does not require training). It also produced the lowest RMSE values for TICs in artery (0.12), venous (0.14), and white matter (0.15) regions among all compared methods. In terms of global registration accuracy, C2FViT achieved the best performance, with DC values of 0.98, 0.97, and 0.82 for white matter, gray matter and cerebrospinal fluid, respectively, and the lowest HD95 value (9.5). The proposed TIC-SViT achieved the second best performance, with DC values of 0.97, 0.96, and 0.81, and HD95 of 10.2. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed method demonstrated registration accuracy comparable to that of state-of-the-art methods, but with significant improvement in computational efficiency.

articles.title: Impacts of Retrospective Lipid Suppression on Metabolite Quantification in Preclinical Proton MR Spectroscopic Imaging.
articles.abstract: Extracranial lipid contamination remains a challenge in proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI), especially in short acquisition delay MRSI, where broad lipid resonances overlap with metabolite and macromolecular signals. Although retrospective lipid suppression techniques are widely used in human MRSI, their effects on metabolite quantification in preclinical MRSI, which is more prone to lipid contamination, have not yet been examined. In this study, we assessed how the retrospective lipid suppression and spectral fitting range influence spectral quality, spatial metabolite mapping, and quantification variability using proton MRSI of rat brains at 14.1 T. Lipid suppression was applied via an orthogonal projection method to both fully sampled and compressed sensing datasets, each comprising data with minimal and pronounced lipid contamination. Spectral fitting was performed with both broad (4.1-0.2 ppm) and narrow (4.1-1.8 ppm) ranges. When lipid contamination was minimal, suppression caused only slight spectral and spatial changes, with consistent metabolite quantification across conditions. In contrast, datasets with pronounced lipid contamination exhibited notable spectral changes following suppression, consequently affecting spatial metabolite mapping and concentration estimates. Group analysis revealed that metabolites with low concentration estimates were most affected. Similar effects were observed in compressed sensing datasets. Our results provide a better understanding of the impact of retrospective lipid suppression on metabolite quantification in preclinical MRSI, thereby supporting future optimizations for its effective application.

articles.title: High-Resolution 3D UTE MRI for Integrated Radiation-Free Pulmonary and Osseous Thoracic Imaging.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study is to propose a three-dimensional ultrashort echo time (3D UTE) MRI technique for integrated, radiation-free thoracic imaging and evaluate its performance for simultaneous visualization of pulmonary and osseous thoracic structures. Five volunteers were scanned on a clinical 3-T MRI system using respiratory-gated 3D UTE and zero echo time (ZTE) sequences. UTE and ZTE were compared at matched 1.6-mm isotropic resolution to assess image quality. UTE acquisitions were further performed at isotropic resolutions of 1.6, 1.4, and 1.2 mm to determine the optimal balance between spatial resolution and clinically feasible scan time. The effects of respiratory gating were evaluated by comparing gated and free-breathing acquisitions. Contrast inversion and multistructure segmentation were applied to generate CT-like bone images and 3D renderings of the lungs, rib cage, and spine. Compared with ZTE, UTE provided more homogeneous signal intensity; reduced excitation-related artifacts; and improved delineation of pulmonary vasculature, airways, and vertebral cortical bone. Increasing spatial resolution progressively improved visualization of fine pulmonary and osseous structures, with 1.2-mm isotropic resolution yielding the highest image quality while maintaining a clinically acceptable scan time of ~7 min. Respiratory gating further improved image sharpness by reducing motion-related blurring, particularly in the lungs. The optimized UTE acquisition enabled simultaneous high-resolution visualization of lung parenchyma, ribs, and spine and supported successful 3D segmentation and rendering of multiple thoracic structures from a single dataset. The proposed 3D UTE MRI enables high-resolution, simultaneous imaging of pulmonary and osseous thoracic anatomy within a single radiation-free examination. Compared with ZTE, UTE demonstrated superior image quality and structural delineation, supporting its potential as a comprehensive alternative to CT for integrated thoracic assessment.

articles.title: EffNetV2M-ViT: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for MRI-Based Differentiation of Glioblastoma and Brain Metastasis.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive differentiation between glioblastoma (GBM) and brain metastasis (BM) remains challenging because of substantial overlap in their MRI appearance. Existing deep learning (DL) approaches have primarily relied on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which capture local spatial features, or transformer-based models, which capture long-range contextual relationships. However, the complementary value of combining these representations for GBM-BM discrimination has not been sufficiently investigated, using independently validated multicenter data. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer (ViT) framework for automated differentiation of GBM from BM. The framework integrates EfficientNet-based convolutional feature extraction with ViT-based global feature modeling through parallel fusion. Enhancing tumor was automatically segmented using 3D U-Net, with segmentations visually reviewed and manually corrected when necessary. T2-weighted (T2W) and contrast enhanced T1-weighted (CE-T1W) MRI sequences were used as inputs. A modality ablation study was performed to identify the optimal contrast combination among T1W, CE-T1W, T2W, and FLAIR. The framework was evaluated in a retrospective cohort of 344 patients with histologically confirmed tumors using cross-validation and ensemble methods, with performance further assessed in an independent multicenter external validation cohort from different institutions, MRI scanner platforms, and patient populations. The hybrid EffNetV2M-ViT framework achieved an accuracy of 95.4%, F1-score of 96.2%, and AUC of 98.4% on the internal test set, and 90.9%, 92.7%, and 96.8% on external validation, with sensitivity, specificity of 96.2%, 93.9% and 90.5%, 91.7%, respectively. The hybrid model outperformed the standalone CNN and ViT models across both datasets, with the largest performance gains observed in the external validation cohort, support its generalizability. Ablation analysis confirmed that the paired CE-T1W + T2W input yielded the most consistent performance across both cohorts, with additional contrasts providing no added benefit. These findings suggest that combining local convolutional features with global contextual representations improves automated GBM-BM discrimination, offering a noninvasive, standardized approach for MRI-based tumor classification that may support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Improving Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF) Mapping From Integrated Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping and Quantitative Blood Oxygen Level Dependent Imaging (QSM+qBOLD, or QQ) by Learning Temporal Signal Evolution.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To improve deep learning-based QSM+qBOLD (QQ) oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) mapping by explicitly learning the temporal evolution of the multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) magnitude signal, whose decay encodes the tissue oxygenation that QQ-based OEF mapping depends on. METHODS: 3D multi-echo gradient echo images were acquired in 34 ischemic stroke patients with arterial spin labeling (ASL) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). We developed QQ-S, a deep learning method that estimates OEF by inverting the QQ model. QQ-S extends QQ-NET by adding convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) modules to the encoder to process the mGRE echoes sequentially. To isolate the effect of this architectural change, both networks were trained with the same simulated data and training scheme including the loss function. OEF maps from QQ-S and QQ-NET were compared in simulation and ischemic stroke patients. RESULTS: In simulation, QQ-S provided more accurate OEF than QQ-NET, with lower mean absolute error (MAE) against the simulation ground truth: 3.43% vs. 5.03% in normal-appearing tissue and 4.88% vs. 10.60% in low-OEF lesions. In subacute stroke patients, where no ground truth is available, the lesion-to-contralateral OEF ratio was significantly lower with QQ-S than with QQ-NET (0.71 ± 0.26 vs. 0.81 ± 0.24; p < 0.001), suggesting more sensitive detection of lesion OEF, consistent with PET reports in the subacute phase. OEF in acute lesions and normal-appearing tissue was comparable between methods. CONCLUSION: By explicitly learning inter-echo signal evolution with ConvLSTM, QQ-S improves OEF accuracy over QQ-NET, offering a promising tool for assessing tissue viability from conventional mGRE data.

articles.title: A prospective comparison of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for evaluating viable brain metastases in lung cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Standard [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT has suboptimal sensitivity for assessing viable brain metastases due to high physiological brain background. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted PET, with minimal brain expression, may overcome this limitation. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 versus [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT for detecting viable brain metastases in lung cancer and evaluate their complementary value. METHODS: In this prospective intra-individual study, 24 lung cancer patients with brain metastases underwent both [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 and [¹⁸F]FDG PET/CT within 3 days. Images were independently and blindly reviewed by two senior nuclear medicine physicians. Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy) was evaluated per-lesion and per-patient against a composite reference standard (characteristic imaging features, ≥ 3-month follow-up, comprehensive clinical evaluation). Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, target-to-background ratio [TBR], background uptake [SUVbgd]) and complementary detection patterns were analyzed. RESULTS: Among 43 lesions (36 viable, 7 non-viable), [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 demonstrated significantly higher per-lesion sensitivity (83.3% vs. 75.0%, P = 0.032) and accuracy (86.0% vs. 79.1%, P = 0.002) than [¹⁸F]FDG. Per-patient sensitivity (89.5% vs. 73.7%, P = 0.004) and accuracy (91.7% vs. 79.2%, P = 0.003) were also superior. The AUC for [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 was 0.917 (95% CI: 0.834-0.999) versus 0.875 (95% CI: 0.772-0.978) for [¹⁸F]FDG (P = 0.031). [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 provided dramatically higher TBR in viable lesions (85.39 ± 57.99 vs. 5.19 ± 2.56, P < 0.001) due to minimal physiological brain background (SUVbgd 0.09 ± 0.11). Dual-tracer imaging supplemented the detection of 15 viable tumor lesions in 9 patients that were missed by either single tracer alone, increasing per-lesion sensitivity to 100% and preventing potential underdiagnosis in 47.4% (9/19) of patients with viable disease. CONCLUSIONS: [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-2286 PET/CT outperforms [¹⁸F]FDG in identifying viable brain metastases from lung cancer, primarily due to its exceptional tumor-to-background contrast. The complementary detection patterns of the two tracers suggest that combined use can minimize diagnostic omissions, supporting an integrative imaging paradigm for more accurate intracranial staging/restaging. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered 10 October 2022, https://www.chictr.org.cn , ChiCTR2100044131.

articles.title: Anatomy-Based Simulations of B0 Field Maps: A Large Database for Head and Spine Shim Coil Development.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Static magnetic field (B0) inhomogeneity degrades MRI quality near air-tissue interfaces in the brain and spine. Anatomically tailored shim coils can mitigate these effects, but their design requires knowledge of B0 distributions across diverse human anatomies and realistic posture differences. This study aimed to create an open-source database of simulated B0 field maps derived from segmented MRI to support brain and spine shimming development. METHODS: Sixty volunteers were scanned at two 3T sites using T1-weighted MPRAGE protocols with head-to-torso coverage. Anatomical structures were segmented using three automated tools (Samseg, TotalSpineSeg, and a custom nnU-Net v2 model) to label the body, brain, skull, spine, vertebrae, discs, sinuses, trachea, and lungs. Segmentations were post-processed using a custom 3D Slicer pipeline for island removal, hole filling, and smoothing, then merged and assigned literature-based susceptibility values. ΔB0 maps were simulated via Fourier-domain convolution with the dipole kernel. Simulations were compared against measured field maps in two additional subjects. To illustrate an application, volume-wise and slice-wise shimming were performed on this simulated dataset. RESULTS: Expected inhomogeneity patterns were observed in simulated ΔB0 maps near airways. The subject-averaged spatial standard deviation of ΔB0 within the brain was reduced by 66.7% with whole-volume second-order shimming and by 70.9% with subsequent first-order slice-wise shimming. CONCLUSION: An open-source database of 60 anatomy-based simulated ΔB0 maps spanning the brain and spinal cord for shimming optimization is presented, with all data and code publicly available.

articles.title: High-Resolution Multi-Delay Renal Arterial Spin Labeling Using Radial Imaging at 5T MRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a high-resolution multi-delay renal arterial spin labeling (ASL) technique for free-breathing imaging at 5T. METHODS: A radial renal ASL (Radial-ASL) sequence was proposed using flow-sensitive alternating inversion recovery (FAIR) preparation followed by continuous golden-angle radial acquisition. The k-space data were firstly sorted by delay time and then reordered based on respiratory motion, with data grouped into four respiratory phases for Spatio-Temporal eXtra-Dimensional Golden-angle RAdial Sparse Parallel (ST-XD-GRASP) reconstruction. Both the Buxton kinetic model and a stepwise kinetic model were applied to perfusion quantification. The proposed method was evaluated against the saturated multi-delay ASL (SAMURAI) technique using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and correlation analysis. Scan-rescan repeatability and interobserver reproducibility were assessed using ICC. RESULTS: Twelve healthy volunteers (mean age: 27.4 ± 4.9 years old, 7 males) and one patient (55-year-old female) were included. Radial-ASL with ST-XD-GRASP provided high-quality images with 1.17 mm in-plane resolution. The stepwise model showed improved fitting performance (R2 ≥ 0.95) compared with the Buxton model (R2: 0.36-0.85). Cortical renal blood flow showed no significant difference between Radial-ASL and SAMURAI (363.7 ± 30.3 vs. 360.4 ± 30.0 mL/100 g/min, p = 0.216), with good agreement (ICC = 0.910) and strong correlation (r = 0.912). Radial-ASL demonstrated good scan-rescan repeatability (ICC = 0.884-0.911) and interobserver reproducibility (ICC = 0.943-0.985). CONCLUSION: Radial-ASL at 5T enables free-breathing multi-delay renal perfusion quantification with high spatial resolution and demonstrates good agreement with SAMURAI technique as well as good repeatability.

articles.title: Importance of Background Suppression and Post Label Delay Optimization for White Matter Perfusion Imaging Using Arterial Spin Labeling at 7 Tesla.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Ultra-high field MRI (7 Tesla) could potentially improve white matter (WM) perfusion imaging because of less severe loss of label thanks to longer T1-values. However, physiological noise increases, making background suppression (BGS) likely more important at this field strength. The aim of this study is first to assess the importance of background suppression at 7 Tesla compared to 3 Tesla, and secondly to use that knowledge to optimize flow-alternating-inversion-recovery (FAIR) ASL for WM perfusion imaging. METHODS: A background suppressed FAIR ASL labeling scheme was implemented at both 7 and 3 Tesla scanners. Perfusion temporal SNR was compared over a wide range of BGS-levels by exploiting a 2D multi-slice readout. The knowledge gained from this was used to optimize a FAIR ASL scan with 3D readout scanned at several post label delays (PLD). The tSNR was compared across PLD for GM and several WM masks. RESULTS: BGS was found to be more important at 7 Tesla compared to 3 Tesla. Therefore, a 3D FAIR ASL scan with homogeneous high BGS was used for WM perfusion imaging. Across PLD, we found a parabolic trend for significant voxels in the deep WM, both for a non-zero but slightly stronger for the ischemic perfusion threshold, peaking around a PLD of 2300 ms. However, this was not significantly higher than a PLD of 1800 and 2800 ms in this healthy population. CONCLUSION: BGS becomes increasingly important for perfusion imaging at higher field strengths. Background suppressed WM perfusion imaging at 7 Tesla might benefit from a longer PLD than typically recommended for GM.

articles.title: Pulsed Off-Resonance Saturation for Macromolecular Proton Fraction-Weighted Contrast With Intrinsic Flow Attenuation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a pulsed off-resonance magnetization transfer (MT) preparation module that achieves intrinsic flow attenuation while enabling efficient macromolecular proton fraction (MPF)-weighted contrast that specific to macromolecular pool. METHODS: In the proposed MPF-SPS (MPF-weighted contrast mapping using short pulsed saturation) approach, repetitive short off-resonance RF pulses are applied in conjunction with spoiler gradients, enabling simultaneous MT contrast generation in stationary tissue and intrinsic blood signal attenuation. An MPF-weighted relaxation rate,  R mpfsps   , is derived that is specific to the macromolecular pool and independent of the free water pool. An off-resonance Extended Phase Graph (EPG) framework incorporating MT effects was developed for efficient parameter optimization. The proposed approach is validated with EPG-based two-pool simulations, phantom, and in vivo brain studies at 3.0 T. RESULTS: Simulations showed that the off-resonance EPG-MT framework closely agrees with two-pool Bloch-McConnell simulations while requiring substantially less computation time. This efficient framework was used to optimize the sequence parameters, confirming that intrinsic flow attenuation effectively reduces partial-volume effects caused by intravascular signal contamination. Both simulations and phantom experiments demonstrated that MPF-SPS provides  R mpfsps   maps that are insensitive to free-water-pool parameters. In vivo brain imaging further demonstrated that the proposed method generates  R mpfsps   maps with MPF-weighted contrast and intrinsic flow attenuation. CONCLUSION: A novel MPF-weighted contrast imaging method using pulsed off-resonance MT preparation with intrinsic flow attenuation is proposed, providing a technical basis for future MPF-sensitive vessel wall imaging.

articles.title: A Dataset-Conditioned Visual State-Space Model with Clinical Taxonomy and Mask Guidance for Multi-Dataset Cystoscopic Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Classification of bladder lesions in cystoscopic images is difficult because datasets differ in acquisition conditions and label spaces, classes are imbalanced, and non-lesion regions can dominate the image. We propose Dataset-Conditioned Clinical-Taxonomy-Gated VMamba (DCTG-VMamba), a visual state-space model that jointly learns CystoDS, the Endoscopic Bladder Tissue Classification dataset (EBTC), and Kaggle white-light imaging (WLI) using supervision from a shared research taxonomy without clinical expert validation and dataset-conditioned fusion of mask-derived region-of-interest (ROI) and surrounding-context tokens with a global image token. After cleaning, 8067, 1611, and 1229 images were analyzed, respectively, using five-fold cross-validation with disjoint patient, file-derived case, or image groups. Three joint-training multiclass and three separately trained binary tasks were evaluated. Models included eight reference backbones, DCTG-VMamba, five prespecified ablations, and dataset-specific VMamba-T controls. The evaluation comprised 535 training runs covering primary classification, ablations, supervision-matched binary controls, and source-held-out transfer. In the initial experiments, DCTG-VMamba achieved macro-F1 scores of 0.609 ± 0.075, 0.590 ± 0.136, and 0.958 ± 0.005 on five-class CystoDS, four-class EBTC, and six-class Kaggle WLI. Repeated experiments did not establish a consistent advantage over joint VMamba-T, and the initial EBTC mean ranking was not reproduced. Binary-label-only DCTG-VMamba had higher observed macro-F1 than joint VMamba-T in all three binary tasks, but no paired difference was significant after Holm correction. Auxiliary mask supervision showed a consistent descriptive direction on CystoDS, and validation-fitted temperature scaling reduced EBTC calibration error. Transfer comparisons showed no consistent advantage over joint VMamba-T. The contribution is a unified learning framework and its controlled evaluation across heterogeneous cystoscopic label spaces.

articles.title: Multimodal Integration of Imaging and Pathological Features for Postoperative Outcome Prediction in Liver Cancer.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to construct and externally validate a multimodal radiopathomic fusion model for predicting postoperative recurrence in patients with primary liver cancer (restricted to hepatocellular carcinoma, excluding intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and mixed-type hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) after curative hepatectomy, and to explore its independent prognostic efficacy and clinical utility. A total of 280 primary liver cancer patients from two centers were retrospectively allocated to a training cohort (n = 182) and an independent validation cohort (n = 98). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative abdominal MRI, while pathomic features were quantified from H&E-stained whole-slide images. Eight machine learning algorithms were screened via fivefold cross‑validation for unimodal model development. The optimal random forest classifier was applied to construct unimodal radiomic‑only and pathomic‑only models, whereas the final multimodal fusion model was built using logistic regression with concatenated pre‑screened radiomic and pathomic features. ROC, SHAP, Kaplan-Meier survival, and logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess model performance, risk stratification, and independent predictors. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two cohorts. We extracted 3390 MRI radiomic and 1039 pathomic features and then built single-modal and fusion models. The fusion model outperformed unimodal models (AUC = 0.894 training, 0.858 validation). It stratified patients into low-/high-recurrence risk subgroups (HR = 9.93 and 5.32). Multivariable analysis confirmed Fusion_Risk score (HR = 18.73) as the strongest independent recurrence predictor, superior to routine clinicopathological biomarkers. The radiopathomic fusion model showed good calibration and satisfactory net clinical benefit. Compared with unimodal models, it exhibited a trend toward improved predictive performance, suggesting potential value as an independent prognostic tool for individualized postoperative recurrence surveillance in patients with primary liver cancer after curative resection.

articles.title: DiCoNet: Diagnosis-Conditioned Report Generation for Retinal OCT via Pseudo Semantic Embedding.
articles.abstract: Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) report generation faces two major challenges: the scarcity of paired image-report data and the inherent semantic gap between visual representations and clinical concepts. Under such low-resource conditions, conventional vision-driven encoder-decoder models are prone to representation degradation and pathological hallucination, which cause semantic drift and make generated reports deviate from true clinical diagnoses. Inspired by the diagnostic workflow in clinical practice, where diagnosis precedes description, we propose a diagnosis-conditioned network, DiCoNet, which reformulates medical report generation from direct image-text mapping into a diagnosis-conditioned sequence generation task. DiCoNet adopts a two-stage progressive training strategy. It first learns robust and discriminative visual representations from a large-scale diagnostic classification dataset and then performs partial fine-tuning on limited report data. To bridge the gap between visual representations and diagnostic semantics, we design a pseudo semantic embedding (PSE) module that injects continuous diagnostic priors directly into the visual prefix, guiding report generation without increasing the prefix length. We further introduce an auxiliary diagnostic supervision branch to maintain feature discriminability during decoding and enable end-to-end autonomous inference without external labels at test time. Extensive experiments on a real-world clinical OCT dataset show that DiCoNet achieves the best scores among the evaluated methods on most automatic evaluation metrics, with a ROUGE-L score of 0.420 and a CIDEr score of 0.951. Expert evaluation and an OCT-specific clinical error analysis further support the accuracy and completeness of DiCoNet-generated reports, highlighting its potential for assisting OCT report drafting.

articles.title: A Deep Learning Framework Integrating Multi-Region Radiomics and Clinical Features for Improved Breast Ultrasound Lesion Classification.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer poses a substantial global burden on women's health, making accurate early differentiation of benign and malignant breast lesions essential for improving prognosis and reducing healthcare costs. Although deep learning methods have been widely developed for breast ultrasound lesion classification, most rely on imaging information alone. Existing approaches incorporating peritumoral information often use empirically defined regions, while clinical characteristics are rarely integrated into end-to-end frameworks, limiting the use of complementary diagnostic information. To address these limitations, we propose Multi-Source Information Fusion DenseNet (MSIF-DenseNet), an end-to-end framework for breast ultrasound lesion classification. It jointly integrates intratumoral ultrasound images, peritumoral regions, and structured clinical information. Specifically, a dual-stream convolutional architecture with separable convolutions independently learns representative features from the intratumoral and peritumoral regions, while a multi-layer perceptron branch encodes patient clinical characteristics. The resulting imaging and clinical features are subsequently fused through a Compact Bilinear Pooling (CBP) module to capture high-order interactions among heterogeneous information sources for benign-malignant classification. On a private dataset comprising 500 breast ultrasound images from 500 patients, MSIF-DenseNet achieved an AUC of 84.21 % ± 3.52 %  , F1-score of 83.81 % ± 3.40 %  , and accuracy of 80.00 % ± 3.90 %  under five-fold cross-validation. Compared with the imaging-only dual-stream baseline, integrating clinical information increased AUC and F1-score by 4.13 and 2.69 percentage points (pp), respectively, while integration of multi-region information increased AUC and F1-score by 9.86 and 6.09 pp, respectively, over the best single-region model. These results support the effectiveness of combining multi-region ultrasound information with clinical data for breast ultrasound lesion classification.

articles.title: Reducing Demographic Bias in Medical Imaging Using Siamese Representation Learning.
articles.abstract: Deep learning models for medical imaging often exhibit demographic bias, leading to performance disparities across protected groups such as age, gender, and race. This study proposes a debiasing framework to reduce such disparities while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. We propose a Siamese neural network trained using triplet loss, where demographic attributes are incorporated into triplet selection to encourage separation by disease class while promoting within-class similarity across demographic groups. The method was evaluated on pleural effusion detection using chest X-rays (109,005 images from 41,063 patients) and Alzheimer's disease classification using brain MRI (1494 scans from 348 patients). Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), precision, and true positive rate, along with equalized odds difference. The proposed method significantly reduced demographic disparities while maintaining or improving overall predictive performance compared with baseline and existing debiasing approaches. In pleural effusion detection, true positive rate gaps were reduced by 32% (race), 8% (age), and 22% (gender). In Alzheimer's disease classification, the true positive rate gap was reduced by 41% (age). Model interpretation indicated clinically meaningful imaging features were used for decision-making. Demographic-aware triplet sampling within a Siamese framework can effectively mitigate demographic performance disparities in medical imaging models while maintaining competitive overall diagnostic performance, suggesting potential for more equitable and clinically reliable deployment of medical imaging AI systems.

articles.title: Knowledge-Guided Fine-Grained Self-Supervised Multimodal Representation Learning for MRI-Visible Endolymphatic Hydrops Assessment in Ménière's Disease.
articles.abstract: Ménière's disease (MD) is a clinically defined inner-ear disorder with heterogeneous manifestations, for which MRI-visible endolymphatic hydrops (EH) is an imaging finding rather than a sufficient diagnostic criterion. We developed a multimodal pretraining framework that combines anatomically constrained representation learning from inner-ear MRI with ontology-normalized concepts extracted from radiology reports. Evaluation used five patient-disjoint outer folds comprising 524 patients (1048 ears) and focused on ear-level MRI-visible EH assessment rather than MD diagnosis. With 10% of the downstream labels, SMAM-MD achieved an AUC of 87.95 ± 1.84 %  , 3.30 percentage points above the strongest displayed baseline mean; under full supervision, its AUC was 98.40 ± 0.72 %  , compared with 98.65 ± 0.65 %  for DINOv2 FT. For prediction of six discharge hearing thresholds from inner-ear MRI and admission audiometry, SMAM-MD achieved an overall macro-MAE of 6.83 ± 0.33   dB HL, compared with 7.47 ± 0.36   dB HL for DINOv2 FT (Holm-adjusted P = 0.000570  ). These findings support improved label efficiency and lower discharge-threshold prediction error within this single-center cohort; they do not establish MRI-based MD diagnosis, causal treatment effects, or external clinical generalizability.

articles.title: Retinex Algorithm-Based Automated Quantification of Eight Key Reflux Signs and Overall Score of Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease.
articles.abstract: The Reflux Finding Score (RFS) is a widely used laryngoscopy-based instrument for assessing laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD); however, its reliance on subjective interpretation leads to considerable inter-observer variability. In this study, we propose TM-Net, a computer-vision framework for automated LPRD assessment. To address three key clinical challenges in automated RFS scoring-uneven illumination, robust feature representation, and anatomically grounded fine-grained scoring-TM-Net integrates three key components. First, MSRCR-based image enhancement normalizes illumination variations and enhances subtle pathological signs. Second, a ResNet-50 encoder with a local self-attention (LSA) module extracts robust features and captures both local and global representations. Third, a segmentation network (TS-Net) delineates seven laryngeal anatomical regions to provide explicit spatial priors, and a feature fusion strategy (CLIA) combined with a multi-label classification network (MLC-Net) simultaneously predicts item-specific ordinal scores for all eight RFS sub-items according to the RFS criteria, enabling fine-grained quantification instead of coarse binary classification. These designs improve performance by addressing illumination variations, enhancing feature representation, and imposing anatomical constraints for comprehensive sub-item scoring. TS-Net achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.7975 and an F1 score of 0.8581 across seven laryngeal regions. Using 24-h multichannel intraluminal impedance-pH monitoring as the reference standard, TM-Net achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 90.91%, with substantial agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.75) and no significant discordance (McNemar's test, P = 1.000). These results indicate that TM-Net provides an objective and standardized tool for LPRD screening.

articles.title: A Dual-View Context-Aware Framework for Automated Bone Lesion Segmentation and Quantification in Whole-Body Planar Bone Scintigraphy.
articles.abstract: Whole-body planar bone scintigraphy reflects skeletal metabolic activity throughout the body and is widely used for the assessment of bone metastases. However, automatic segmentation of hypermetabolic bone lesions remains challenging because of low image contrast, limited spatial resolution, and complex lesion distributions. In this study, we proposed a dual-view context-aware framework that employed Bone-Segnet, a segmentation network integrating multiscale feature modeling, global context modeling, and view-conditioned modulation to improve lesion representation and segmentation. The study included whole-body planar bone scintigraphy images from 932 patients, with hypermetabolic bone lesions manually delineated on anterior and posterior images by experienced nuclear medicine physicians. The proposed network effectively segmented hypermetabolic bone lesions with complex distributions. In performance comparisons, it achieved the best segmentation performance among the evaluated baseline models, with the dice score showing the largest improvement from 0.7440 to 0.8750. In a preliminary reader efficiency evaluation involving two experienced nuclear medicine physicians, the average annotation time decreased from 38.20 s/image to 18.41 s/image under a model-assisted workflow involving automatic segmentation followed by manual correction, representing a 51.81% reduction. Quantitative analysis of the segmentation results yielded image-derived descriptors, including connected-component counts and total segmented pixel counts, across disease types. These results suggest that the proposed framework achieves improved segmentation performance for hypermetabolic bone lesions relative to the evaluated baseline models and may reduce annotation workload, thereby providing a basis for downstream quantitative imaging analysis in whole-body planar bone scintigraphy.

articles.title: Eye-Tracking-Guided Tri-View Learning for Fine-Grained Medical Image Classification and Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Fine-grained medical image analysis involves two core tasks: image-level disease classification and pixel-level border delineation, both requiring intelligent models to capture subtle lesion-relevant visual cues. We investigate a shared gaze-guided multi-view design principle through separate task-specific classification and segmentation models. For classification, gaze heatmaps are used to derive point prompts and construct global, lesion-core, and peri-lesional views, enabling the model to integrate whole-image context, lesion-dominant details, and surrounding tissue information. In addition, a dual-path diagnosis module is designed to combine direct prediction of disease classes with hierarchical lesion-dominant subtype refinement. For segmentation, we introduce Tri-view Gaze-prior Input (TVGP-Input), a plug-and-play input-level module that introduces eye-tracking-derived spatial priors to segmentation backbones without modifying their encoder-decoder structures. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.8680 ± 0.0236  , a macro-F1 score of 0.7255 ± 0.0425  , a weighted F1 score of 0.8531 ± 0.0195  , and macro- and micro-averaged areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.8968 ± 0.0358  and 0.9668 ± 0.0199  in five-fold cross-validation on three-class medical image classification. In segmentation experiments, the proposed TVGP-Input enhanced tri-view segmentation model achieves a Dice score of 0.9285 ± 0.0109  and an intersection over union of 0.8694 ± 0.0144  . These results support gaze-guided learning within the evaluated breast ultrasound classification and prostate magnetic resonance imaging segmentation settings.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Imaging Integration for Individualized Transseptal Puncture Planning During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
articles.abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. In the temporal validation cohort, at least one AI-recommended adjustment was incorporated into the final TSP strategy in 68 patients (34.0%). The recommendations addressed involved three key components of TSP planning: puncture site category in 52 patients (26.0%), puncture direction in 61 patients (30.5%), and puncture trajectory or angle in 74 patients (37.0%). AI-assisted assessment increased decision confidence (4.3 ± 0.6 vs. 3.4 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), reduced planning time (28.7 ± 10.3 vs. 42.5 ± 15.2 s, p < 0.001), and improved interreader agreement for anatomical assessment. In the temporal validation cohort, acute successful TSP was achieved in 196 patients (98.0%), with a mean transseptal time of 6.8-2.5 min and an overall complication rate of 3.0%. AI-assisted integration of preprocedural CTA with intraoperative ICE provides patient-specific 3D anatomical information that supports individualized TSP planning. The proposed framework demonstrated feasibility and compatibility with anatomical assessment and procedural planning, hopefully contributing to improve procedural or clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Spectral Decorrelation of Glutamate for Clinical Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Although glutamate (Glu) plays a central role in many neuropsychiatric disorders, MRS measurement of Glu often suffers from confounding correlations due to spectral overlap, adversely affecting subsequent clinical correlational analysis. This study aimed to optimize the commonly used 3 T PRESS method to minimize the overall Glu spectral correlation with other neurometabolites. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations combined with a mathematical model of spectral fitting were used to evaluate spectral correlations between Glu and other metabolites. The optimal {TE1, TE} pair minimizing the overall Glu correlation was identified and validated by analyzing in vivo measurement of Glu in the anterior cingulate cortex. The robustness of the optimization was further assessed under varying spectral linewidths and altered metabolite concentrations. RESULTS: The optimal {TE1, TE} values for 4, 6, 8, and 10 Hz linewidth were found to be {42, 100}, {40, 95}, {38, 94}, and {38, 90} ms, respectively. These optimal {TE1, TE} pairs reduced the overall Glu spectral correlation coefficient to less than 0.05, corresponding to a negligible effect size. This reduction was consistently observed in both Monte Carlo simulations and analysis of in vivo measurements and remained robust across metabolite level variations typically seen in bipolar disorder, methamphetamine use disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and hepatic encephalopathy. CONCLUSION: Systematic optimization of the {TE1, TE} pair enables decorrelation of Glu MRS measurement at 3 Tesla by effectively minimizing confounding spectral correlations among brain metabolites. The proposed approach provides a robust and clinically applicable framework that decorrelates Glu MRS measurements for viable downstream clinical analyses.

articles.title: Quantifying inter-surgeon variation in computed tomography-based preoperative planning for total hip arthroplasty.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Three-dimensional (3D) preoperative planning is essential in total hip arthroplasty (THA) to optimize implant alignment and reduce the risk of impingement-related complications such as dislocation. Although recent technological advances, including computed tomography (CT)-based navigation and robotic-assisted surgery, have improved the accuracy of implant placement, variation in preoperative planning among surgeons remains poorly understood. This study aimed to quantify inter-surgeon variation in 3D preoperative THA planning and to evaluate the impact of stem design on this variation. METHODS: Eleven hip surgeons independently performed 3D preoperative planning for 50 THA cases using a CT-based planning system. The cases included two stem types: tapered wedge stems and anatomical stems. Implant size was fixed, and planning was performed according to the combined anteversion theory. Inter-surgeon variation in implant orientation and position was quantified using the mean pairwise absolute difference (MPD) and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC). The surgeon-selected cup-stem anteversion combinations were grouped into five categories, and inter-surgeon agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa coefficient. RESULTS: Angular MPDs ranged from 0.8° to 3.8°, with the greatest variation observed in stem anteversion. Positional MPDs ranged from 0.8 to 2.1 mm, with the largest variation observed along the stem craniocaudal axis. The ICCs ranged from 0.69 to 0.99. Agreement in cup-stem anteversion categories was moderate (kappa = 0.44). When the two stem groups were compared, no significant differences in angular variation were observed, while only limited differences in positional variation were found. CONCLUSION: Inter-surgeon variation assessed by MPD provided a direct measure of the absolute magnitude of differences among surgeons' plans. Our findings demonstrate that noticeable inter-surgeon variation exists in preoperative THA planning despite high agreement coefficients. Quantitative benchmarks derived from these data may be useful for evaluating planning consistency and for validating emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-based automated THA planning systems.
